metadata.title: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction and Mental Health: A Bidirectional Relationship.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: New-onset mental health (MH) conditions are a concern for patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction. Patients with pre-existing MH conditions have been observed to experience poorer postoperative outcomes. HYPOTHESIS: Patients with pre-existing MH diagnoses would report poorer outcomes after ACL reconstruction, and non-sport-related injuries would be associated with a greater incidence of new MH diagnoses. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3. METHODS: Adults undergoing ACL reconstruction between October 2016 and October 2023 at a large university-affiliated practice were included. Patients completed the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Global Health and Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcomes Score (KOOS) before surgery, and at multiple postoperative timepoints. MH diagnoses included anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, and other psychiatric conditions documented through medications, International Classification of Diseases, tenth revision codes or chart notes. Continuous and categorical variables were compared using appropriate univariate tests, and mixed-model linear regression was used to compare patient-reported outcomes over time while controlling for patient sex. RESULTS: Out of 365 patients undergoing ACL reconstruction, 50 (13.7%) had a pre-existing MH diagnosis (mean age, 36.42; 84.0% female). Groups did not differ on any scale at baseline except PROMIS Mental Health, which was lower among patients with a pre-existing MH diagnosis (47.3 vs 53.6; P < 0.001). The MH Group reported significantly worse KOOS scores at 2 weeks postoperatively, but no differences were observed thereafter. Among 315 patients without previous history of MH disorder (mean age, 32.90; 52.7% female), 8 (2.5%) developed a new MH diagnosis at 1-year follow-up. Patients aged ≤25 years demonstrated significantly higher baseline KOOS scores than patients >25 years. Among 294 sport-related injuries and 71 non-sport-related injuries, non-sport-related injuries were associated with lower baseline KOOS and PROMIS scores, and higher incidence of new MH diagnoses (7% vs 1.6%; P = 0.02). CONCLUSION: No differences in KOOS outcomes beyond 2 weeks were found between patients with and without a pre-existing MH condition. Furthermore, non-sport-related injuries were associated with a higher rate of new MH diagnoses. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings may help clinicians identify patients who could benefit from additional support during recovery.

metadata.title: Age-Related Patterns of Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs) Symptoms and Key Performance Factors in Adolescent Biathletes.
metadata.abstract: Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs) impairs health and performance, but age-related patterns in its emergence remain unclear. This study examines RED symptoms in adolescent biathletes at season-start and their link to end-of-season performance. A national cross-sectional study including prospective performance registration recruited biathletes to complete validated questionnaires, followed by clinical interviews if eating disorders (EDs) were indicated. Athletes ≥ 18 years were invited for physical laboratory assessments. End-of-season results were retrieved from open records. Analyses were performed by elastic net regression to identify the most stable predictors of performance, which were finally included in a linear regression model. Seventy-two athletes (55% females) with mean (SD) age 17.8 (1.4) years, 13.3 (3.3) training hours/week, and representing median (min, max) tier 3.0 (2, 5) were included. Prevalence in symptoms of low energy availability (LEA) was 18%, REDs 32%, EDs 11% (20% among females), and of depression 15%. Among 28 athletes (43% female) completing laboratory assessments, 11% had low BMD and ≤ 25% had clinical metabolic markers. Symptoms of mental health issues and REDs were more common in females and the older age groups. Higher training volume and low RED severity positively predicted performance, whereas injury/illness-related training absences, cholesterol, and body fat percentage negatively affected race results. RED symptoms are common in young biathletes. Illness/injury-related training absences were frequent and linked to poorer end-of-season performance, underscoring the need for routine screening by health- and performance teams to detect and manage early symptoms of LEA, reduce RED risk, and prevent premature career termination.

metadata.title: Objective Return-to-Sport (RTS) Decision Frameworks for Adolescent Shoulder and Elbow Injuries: Tests, Thresholds and Exercise Targets.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adolescent shoulder and elbow injuries are increasing due to sports specialization and year-round training, yet return-to-sport decisions typically rely on adult-derived heuristics that fail to address the unique physiology, growth plate vulnerability, and recovery needs of developing athletes aged 10-19 years. OBJECTIVE: This review proposes a novel, objective three-pillar RTS framework integrating: (1) foundational tissue capacity, (2) dynamic movement quality and neuromuscular control, and (3) sport-specific load tolerance. We synthesize current evidence to establish provisional, consensus-based adolescent thresholds and provide a practical bedside toolkit for immediate clinical implementation. METHODS: We conducted a narrative synthesis of contemporary original evidence, consensus recommendations, and validation studies relevant to adolescent shoulder and elbow rehabilitation. Evidence was critically appraised for youth-specific validation, with explicit distinction between evidence-based interventions and emerging aspirational technologies requiring prospective adolescent cohort validation. RESULTS: We propose a hybrid benchmarking model combining limb symmetry indices (LSI ≥90%) with population-referenced percentiles (≥25th percentile for age/sex/sport) as provisional, consensus-based thresholds. A three-stage progression is outlined: Clinic-ready (pain-free ROM, isometric IR/ER LSI ≥90%), Training-ready (dynamic rotational LSI ≥90%, preserved scapular kinematics), and Game-ready (sport-specific tolerance with 5% velocity loss during simulated exposure). We provide a low-resource bedside toolkit including belt-stabilized hand-held dynamometry, Closed Kinetic Chain Upper Extremity Stability Test (CKCUEST), Push-Up Plus, Athletic Shoulder positions, seated medicine-ball throw, and simple interval tolerance simulations with specific protocols and thresholds. A stepwise algorithm advances from capacity → movement quality → load tolerance with targeted remediation at each gate. CONCLUSION: Moving beyond time-based or adult-derived heuristics, this objective multidimensional framework aligns tissue recovery with sport-specific demands through quantifiable metrics. While provisional thresholds require further adolescent validation, the framework offers an evidence-guided pathway that mitigates reinjury risk, restores performance, and supports safe reintegration into sport. Implementation requires adolescent-specific normative databases, stakeholder communication, and cost-effective technological integration for equitable adoption.

metadata.title: Orthobiologics in Focus: Current Evidence, Clinical Applications, and Future Directions, A Scoping Review.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Regenerative modalities are increasingly becoming part of orthopedic practice with the use of orthobiologic interventions. These interventions make use of biological approaches to help in repairing the tissues, mitigating nociception, and improving locomotor performance. OBJECTIVE: The current scoping review is a review of the modern literature as of 2020-2025 on orthobiologic therapies. It examines their clinical effectiveness, the strength of supporting evidence, and the development of new progress in musculoskeletal pathology regenerative management. METHODS: A systematic search in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and WoS was done on the articles with their indexes dated between January 2020 and February 2025. The inclusion criteria were human and animal studies that utilized platelet-rich plasma (PRP), (MSCs), bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC), and adipose-derived products strategies using a scaffold only. Synthesis and data extraction were conducted as per PRISMA-ScR standards. RESULTS: Among the 1716 records that had been filtered, 81 studies met inclusion criteria. Most of them were randomized or comparative trials (77% Level I-II evidence), which are evidence of the high methodological quality. PRP was the most commonly researched modality, whereas MSC-based interventions were the most common. CONCLUSION: PRP, MSCs, and BMAC are orthobiologic modalities, which are evidence-based and effective alternatives to promote musculoskeletal healing and regeneration. These interventions supplemented by conventional surgical procedures and rehabilitative interventions yield pain relief, functional restoration, and long-term joint maintenance in a spectrum of orthopedic complications.

metadata.title: Autologous Peripheral Blood-Derived Stem Cells Combined with Platelet-Rich Plasma is Associated With Clinical and Radiological Improvement in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Ruptures-Preliminary Clinical and MRI Findings in 47 Consecutive Patients.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) ruptures are common injuries in young and active individuals and can lead to long-term functional impairment and early onset osteoarthritis. While ACL reconstruction remains the standard of care, recent evidence suggests that spontaneous healing may be possible in selected cases. Regenerative and biologic treatment concepts have therefore gained increasing interest. This study investigates the clinical and radiological outcomes of a stem cell-based regenerative treatment for traumatic ACL ruptures and presents findings as preliminary observational evidence. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective case series, 47 patients with isolated partial and complete traumatic anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) ruptures were treated using a biologic, non-surgical protocol. Diagnosis of an ACL rupture was confirmed by standardized clinical examination (Lachman test, anterior drawer test, and pivot shift test) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which was additionally used to assess rupture morphology and synovial sheath integrity. All patients underwent an ultrasound-guided injection of autologous biologic products derived from peripheral venous blood, consisting of 8 mL of an autologous blood-derived stem cell preparation (BSC), comprising approximately 2-3 mL of concentrated mononuclear cells suspended in 6 mL of autologous platelet-containing plasma, injected directly into the torn ACL. Patients were allowed immediate full weight-bearing without bracing and followed a standardized physiotherapy program. Clinical follow-up was conducted for 12 months, including assessment of pain (VAS), functional outcomes (IKDC, Lysholm), return-to-sport timelines, and MRI-based evaluation of ligament morphology. RESULTS: The mean age of the cohort was 28.1 years (95% CI 26.0-30.2). Functional outcomes improved continuously throughout follow-up, with mean IKDC and Lysholm scores of 93.6 (95% CI 92.4-94.8) and 94.0 (95% CI 92.7-95.3), respectively, at 12 months. Pain levels decreased markedly, reaching a mean VAS score of 0.36 (95% CI 0.19-0.53). Patients returned to running after a mean of 2.19 weeks (95% CI 1.93-2.45), and most resumed their pre-injury activity level by one year. No infections or re-ruptures occurred and only one secondary ACL reconstruction was recorded. Patients with an intact synovial sheath demonstrated faster return to pivoting sports (26.8 vs. 33.2 weeks) compared with patients with a complete ACL rupture. MRI at 3 months showed evidence of improved ligament morphology in all but one patient. CONCLUSIONS: This preliminary case series suggests that stem cell-based biologic stimulation may be associated with functional recovery and radiological improvement in selected patients with ACL ruptures. Prospective controlled trials are required to validate these findings.

metadata.title: Learned helplessness is associated with jump-landing biomechanics following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent biomechanical alterations following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) contribute to reduced functional performance, increased reinjury risk, and diminished joint health. Rehabilitation emphasizes strength and functional restoration; however, neurobehavioral adaptations may persist. Learned helplessness, characterized by reduced motivation, maladaptive biomechanics, and learned non-use of the reconstructed limb, may relate to post-operative neuromuscular control. However, its relationship with dynamic movement after ACLR remains unclear. This study examined the association between learned helplessness and bilateral lower extremity kinematics during jump-landings in individuals following ACLR. METHODS: Thirty-three individuals with primary, unilateral ACLR completed a learned helplessness scale and jump-landing task with three-dimensional lower-extremity kinematics. Sagittal and frontal plane knee and hip angles were assessed at initial contact and peak landing. Correlations and regression analyses examined associations with learned helplessness, controlling for age, sex, and time since surgery. FINDINGS: Participants were 2.78 ± 2.78 years post-ACLR and demonstrated low helplessness scores. Greater learned helplessness was moderately associated with greater peak knee abduction in the ACLR limb (r = 0.564, p = 0.001). Weak associations were also observed with reduced peak hip flexion in the ACLR (r = -0.370, p = 0.048) and contralateral limbs (r = -0.415, p = 0.025), which did not survive sensitivity analyses. Learned helplessness was independently associated with greater peak knee abduction angle in the ACLR limb (B = 0.230, p = 0.007). The overall model accounted for 34.8% of the variance in peak knee abduction. INTERPRETATION: Learned helplessness appears to be associated with frontal plane knee mechanics following ACLR. Consideration of psychological and neurobehavioral constructs in rehabilitation and return-to-sport assessment following ACLR is important.

metadata.title: A Narrative Review of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Graft Choice and Its Influence on Return to Sport.
metadata.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) rupture is among the most common knee injuries in active individuals and can lead to persistent instability, secondary intra-articular damage, and an elevated risk of osteoarthritis. Because return to sport (RTS) is a major goal for most active patients and graft selection remains one of the most debated aspects of ACL reconstruction, this narrative review summarizes the contemporary evidence on how graft choice influences RTS, focusing on the four most common grafts: bone-patellar tendon-bone (BTB), hamstring tendon (HT), quadriceps tendon (QT), and allograft. RECENT FINDINGS: RTS rates range from ~ 65% to 73% at three years and are higher (83-90%) in elite and high-school athletes. In young, active patients, autografts are associated with higher RTS and lower revision rates than allografts, and high-level evidence-including randomized-trial meta-analyses-has not established the superiority of any single autograft. BTB offers reliable bone-to-bone healing and low revision rates; HT reduces donor-site morbidity and anterior knee pain but has variable diameter and possible flexion weakness; and QT is a versatile option with favorable biomechanics, low donor-site morbidity, and encouraging RTS data, including in skeletally immature athletes. RTS is one of several important outcomes after ACL reconstruction, alongside long-term joint health and reinjury prevention. For RTS, the literature supports autograft over allograft in young, active patients while identifying no universally superior autograft. Graft selection should be individualized to patient age, sport, activity level, anatomy, and reinjury risk; the senior author favors QT or BTB autografts for high-demand athletes.

metadata.title: Calf Injuries: Anatomy, Pathology, and Treatment.
metadata.abstract: Calf injuries are common in athletes and typically result in missed time from sport and activities of daily living. The three individual triceps surae muscles can be injured, with differing described mechanisms. Gastrocnemius or plantaris strains tend to occur during sudden explosive movement of the ankle from a dorsiflexed to a plantarflexed position with the knee in extension. Soleus strains typically occur from repetitive dorsiflexion of the ankle with the knee flexed. Imaging modalities such as magnetic resonance imaging and ultrasonography can be helpful in determining the location and grade of injury, which can aid in treatment and return to play timelines. Classically, these injuries have been graded as grade I, II, or III, with grade I having <10% muscle fiber disruption, grade II having >10 to 50% muscle fiber disruption, and grade III having 50 to 100% muscle fiber disruption. The mainstay of treatment for most calf strains is nonsurgical, with surgical management being rare but reported in the literature for isolated grade III ruptures of the medial head of the gastrocnemius. Return to sport and activities requires a graduated physical therapy program focused on restoring tissue length without excessive strain. Recent limited evidence has shown promising results with quicker return to activities and decreased pain with platelet-rich plasma injections.

metadata.title: Platelet-related extracellular vesicles: Therapeutic roles in musculoskeletal disorders.
metadata.abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders are a major cause of pain, disability, and loss of function. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been widely investigated for musculoskeletal repair, and interest has increasingly extended to extracellular vesicle (EV) preparations obtained from platelet-related starting materials. These include EV-enriched preparations collected from isolated platelets or defined platelet concentrates (P-EVs), from PRP (PRP-EVs), and from platelet lysate (PL-EVs). They do not represent the same biological product. Their cellular contributors, co-isolated soluble components, and molecular composition can differ substantially, and the name of the starting material does not prove the origin of every vesicle in the preparation. Preclinical studies nevertheless suggest that these EV preparations can influence inflammatory responses, cartilage metabolism, tendon-cell behavior, and the local repair environment. The strength of this evidence varies with the source material, separation and characterization methods, experimental model, and delivery strategy. This review examines the therapeutic evidence for platelet-related EV preparations in musculoskeletal disorders, while keeping P-EVs, PRP-EVs, PL-EVs, and plasma-derived EVs distinct and considering the methodological limitations that currently restrict comparison and clinical translation.

metadata.title: Dosage and safety of non-invasive brain stimulation for chronic musculoskeletal pain management: a scoping review.
metadata.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To map stimulation targets and dosage parameters used in non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS), including repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), theta-burst stimulation (TBS) and transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) for chronic musculoskeletal pain (CMP), and to synthesise rationale for dosage selection, safety monitoring and adverse event reporting. DESIGN: The scoping review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) and Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, using the Arksey and O'Malley framework. DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE (PubMed), Scopus, Web of Science and Embase were searched from their inception to 16 October 2025. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Studies involving adults with CMP receiving rTMS, TBS or tDCS were eligible if they reported at least one of the following outcomes: stimulation targets, dosage parameters or safety. All study designs were eligible. DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Findings were synthesised descriptively by modality, target, dosage characteristics, rationale for parameter selection and safety monitoring. RESULTS: A total of 123 studies were included, predominantly randomised controlled trials (RCTs) involving fibromyalgia, knee osteoarthritis and chronic low back pain. The primary motor cortex (M1) and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex were the most frequently targeted regions for stimulation. Common protocols used 10 Hz rTMS at 80–120% rest motor threshold and tDCS at 1–2 mA for 20–30 min. Treatment schedule varied substantially, ranging from 1 to 60 sessions, and most delivered at five sessions per week over 2 to 4 weeks. Stimulation targets were justified in 63% of studies, whereas rationales for frequency, intensity and number of sessions were reported inconsistently. The method used for adverse events monitoring was not clearly described in 62% of studies. Among the 113 studies in which participants actually received NIBS, reported adverse events were predominantly mild and transient. However, adverse event ascertainment and reporting were inconsistent and the reported percentages represented the proportion of studies reporting each adverse event rather than participant-level incidence. Therefore, these data do not permit reliable estimation of adverse event frequency. CONCLUSION: Current NIBS dosage for management of CMP remains heterogeneous and driven by empirical experience. Safety reporting is inadequate. Although reported adverse events were predominantly mild and transient, inconsistent adverse event ascertainment and reporting preclude reliable conclusion about the safety profile of NIBS. Greater emphasis on brain network theory-informed targets in people with CMP, systematic and personalised dosage optimisation, and standardised safety reporting is needed to support evidence-based clinical implementation. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: DOI: http://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/8HFBZ.

metadata.title: Biomaterial-assisted culture of mesenchymal stem cells for enhanced extracellular vesicle production and cartilage regeneration: a systematic review.
metadata.abstract: Articular cartilage has limited self-repair capacity, prompting interest in cell-free therapies such as extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). This systematic review assessed whether MSCs cultured with biomaterials produce more EVs, and EVs with greater chondrogenic or cartilage-regenerative efficacy, than MSCs in conventional culture. The publications were searched on PubMed, Scopus, and EBSCO (2016-2026), and the synthesis of the evidence was done narratively, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. From 576 unique records, we included 14 preclinical studies: 12 used biomaterials in a three-dimensional format, and two cultured MSCs on decellularized extracellular matrix. Eleven compared biomaterial-culture EVs head-to-head with conventional-culture EVs for chondrogenic or cartilage-repair outcomes. EV yield was higher with the biomaterial in all ten studies that compared it (about 1.2- to 7.5-fold per cell or per unit of protein). In all 11 comparisons, biomaterial-culture EVs matched or exceeded conventional-culture EVs in chondrocyte proliferation, chondrogenic marker expression, matrix deposition, or in vivo cartilage repair. Cargo-target mechanisms were functionally validated in six studies, although in one the microRNA had been enriched by transfection rather than by the culture platform. Certainty of evidence was low for yield and very low for chondrogenic, cartilage-repair, and anti-inflammatory outcomes. Risk of bias was probably low in seven studies and probably high in seven. The comparator arms often differed in more than the biomaterial, and EV characterization was frequently incomplete. In conclusion, biomaterial-assisted culture is a promising but not yet standardized route to more chondrogenic MSC-derived EVs and requires further study.

metadata.title: AAOS Clinical Practice Guidelines for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: Synopsis and Practice Implications.
metadata.abstract: DESCRIPTION: Carpal tunnel syndrome is a common peripheral nerve compression frequently encountered in primary care and internal medicine settings. The American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS) developed updated evidence-based clinical practice guidelines in 2024 to improve outcomes and optimize diagnosis and management. This synopsis highlights recommendations most relevant to nonoperative clinicians, with an emphasis on efficient diagnosis, management, and appropriate referral. METHODS: The AAOS guideline was developed by a multidisciplinary panel using a systematic review of the available literature. Guideline development involved reviewing the evidence, formulating recommendations, and grading them based on the strength of evidence and consensus, in line with established standards for trustworthy clinical practice guidelines. RECOMMENDATIONS: The guidelines emphasize that carpal tunnel syndrome is a clinical diagnosis based on characteristic symptoms and examination findings. Strong evidence supports the use of validated clinical tools, such as the Carpal Tunnel Syndrome-6 (CTS-6), in patients with typical presentations, without routine reliance on ultrasonography or electrodiagnostic testing, which may be reserved for diagnostic uncertainty or potentially recurrent cases. Nonoperative therapies may provide short-term symptom relief; for example, corticosteroid injection demonstrates short-term benefit but does not alter the long-term disease course. Many commonly used interventions, including therapeutic ultrasound, oral corticosteroids, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and platelet-rich plasma injections, lack evidence of clinical benefit and thus are not recommended. Surgical carpal tunnel release, when pursued for moderate to severe symptoms, thenar atrophy, or failure of nonoperative management, may be performed via open or endoscopic release. The guidelines recommend against routine pre-operative testing in otherwise healthy patients. These recommendations support efficient diagnosis, appropriate management, and timely referral while reducing unnecessary testing and low-value care.

metadata.title: Acute and Chronic Effects of Parachute-Resisted Sprint Training on Sprint Performance and Sprint Mechanics: A Systematic Review with GRADE Assessment.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parachute-resisted sprint training (PRST) is a practical field-based resisted-sprint method that uses aerodynamic drag to provide sprint-specific overload. Although PRST has been widely used in athletic settings, evidence on its acute mechanical effects and chronic training adaptations remains heterogeneous. OBJECTIVES: This systematic review aimed to synthesize the acute and chronic effects of PRST on sprint performance, sprint mechanics, neuromuscular responses, and sprint-related physiological outcomes in healthy, physically active, and athletic populations. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and SPORTDiscus on 17th May 2026. Original empirical studies were eligible if they examined PRST or parachute-resisted sprinting and reported outcomes related to sprint performance, biomechanics, neuromuscular responses, or sprint-related physiology. Studies were synthesized narratively and grouped into acute and chronic evidence streams. Methodological quality was assessed using the Modified Downs and Black checklist, and certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE approach. RESULTS: Seventeen studies were included (8 acute and 9 chronic). In acute comparisons, PRST consistently reduced sprint velocity or increased sprint time; where directly reported, velocity reductions were approximately 3.4-6% relative to unresisted sprinting. Larger parachute conditions generally produced greater velocity decrements and changes in horizontal force or impulse variables. Chronic studies reported improvements in selected sprint outcomes, including 0-10 m, 10-20 m, and 0-20 m splits in one randomized study; other studies reported improvements such as 3.48% in 60-yd performance and 0.618 s in 100-m performance. However, chronic studies' findings were heterogeneous, and evidence for maximal velocity, neuromuscular or energetic outcomes, and population-specific effects remained limited. CONCLUSIONS: PRST appears to provide a practical, sprint-specific overload and may improve selected sprint performance outcomes. However, the current evidence base is limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous protocols, poor quantification of resistance, inconsistent reporting of outcomes, and limited comparator control. Based on GRADE, confidence in the evidence is generally 'low' to 'very low' across most outcomes. Trial Registration (OSF) https://osf.io/56nct DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/8SJW4.

metadata.title: Chinese Ethnic Traditional Sports as Mind-Body Interventions for Psychiatric Recovery.
metadata.abstract: Chinese ethnic traditional sports (CETS)-a family of culturally embedded physical practices encompassing traditional Chinese mind-body exercises (e.g., Tai Chi, Qigong, Baduanjin, Yijin Jing, Wuqinxi) and intangible cultural heritage folk sports (e.g., dragon-lion dance)-have attracted growing interest as accessible, low-cost mind-body interventions for mental health. This narrative review examines which mental health outcomes are associated with participation in different types of CETS and to what extent the available evidence supports their role in psychiatric recovery. The review synthesizes 68 studies published between January 2000 and June 2026, identified through multi-database searches of Web of Science, PubMed, and Scopus. Thematic synthesis identified four interconnected dimensions of mental health burden addressed by CETS: (a) affective disorders; (b) trauma-related disorders; (c) sleep-wake disturbances; and (d) cognitive and psychosocial dysfunction. Across these dimensions, individual randomized controlled trials consistently report moderate reductions in depressive and anxiety symptoms, with larger effects when CETS are delivered in supervised groups at moderate intensity for 12-24 weeks; however, most evidence derives from subclinical or non-psychiatric samples and measures symptom severity rather than functional recovery. The review therefore concludes that CETS are a promising, low-cost, culturally congruent adjunct to conventional psychiatric care-warranting rigorous, disorder-specific trials-rather than established stand-alone treatments for psychiatric recovery.

metadata.title: Dose-dependent effects of sodium bicarbonate supplementation combined with sprint interval training on performance adaptations in basketball players: a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sprint interval training (SIT) effectively improves physical performance in team-sport athletes, while sodium bicarbonate (Sb) supplementation may enhance training adaptations. However, the dose-dependent effects of Sb during SIT remain unclear in basketball players. Therefore, this study examined the effects of two Sb doses combined with SIT on physical performance adaptations in basketball players. METHODS: Forty trained male basketball players (age: 21.6 ± 2.0 years, height: 185.4 ± 3.5 cm, body mass: 84.1 ± 4.4 kg) were recruited and randomly assigned to four groups: SIT + 0.3 g·kg-1 Sb (n = 10), SIT + 0.45 g·kg-1 Sb (n = 10), SIT + placebo (PL) (n = 10), and control (CON) (n = 10). The intervention lasted four weeks during the preparatory phase of the season. Participants in the training groups performed SIT three times per week in addition to their regular basketball training. The SIT protocol consisted of four sets of ten 5-second maximal sprints, with 20 seconds of active recovery between repetitions and 2 minutes of rest between sets. All 40 enrolled participants successfully completed the 4-week intervention, resulting in a 0% dropout rate. Performance assessments conducted before and after the intervention included countermovement vertical jump (CMVJ), standing long jump (SLJ), 20 m sprint, Illinois change-of-direction speed (CODS), Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (Yo-Yo IR1), and Wingate anaerobic power (peak power output [PPO] and mean power output [MPO]). RESULTS: All training groups showed significant improvements in physical performance variables over time (p < 0.05). Significant group by time interaction effects were observed for all performance variables (p ≤ 0.001), indicating that the SIT groups showed more gains compared with the CON group. Both Sb supplementation groups demonstrated greater improvements than the SIT + PL group in CMVJ, SLJ, sprint performance, CODS, Yo-Yo IR1 distance, PPO, and MPO (p < 0.05). Furthermore, the SIT + 0.45 g·kg-1 Sb group exhibited significantly greater performance enhancements than the SIT + 0.3 g·kg-1 Sb group across all measured variables. CONCLUSION: Four weeks of SIT improved performance in trained basketball players, with Sb supplementation providing additional dose-dependent benefits (0.45 > 0.3 g⋅kg-1). While the higher dose yielded superior adaptations, its practical application should be balanced against potential gastrointestinal discomfort and individual tolerance to ensure long-term athlete compliance.

metadata.title: Low Physical Therapy Referral Rates for Knee Osteoarthritis Present a Barrier to Care for Patients With Medicaid.
metadata.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the rates of physical therapy (PT) referral for knee osteoarthritis (KOA) and factors associated with referral patterns, including insurance status, provider specialty, year, and patient demographics and comorbidities. DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included 41,373 patients diagnosed with KOA at an integrated health system in Arizona and Colorado, USA between January 2020 and February 2023. PT referral rates were stratified by insurance type. Multivariable logistic regression assessed predictors of referral including insurance type, age, BMI, sex, race/ethnicity, provider specialty, year of visit, and comorbidities. RESULTS: Crude PT referral rates at the initial visit were 12.06% for Medicaid, 6.83% for Medicare, 10.29% for commercial insurance, and 8.33% for uninsured patients. Adjusted analysis showed that Medicaid patients had higher referral odds (OR, 1.20; 95% CI [1.10, 1.30]; p < 0.001), whereas Medicare patients had lower odds (OR, 0.76; 95% CI [0.66, 0.88]; p < 0.001) compared to those with commercial insurance. Female (OR, 1.21; 95% CI [1.14, 1.29]; p < 0.001) and Hispanic patients (OR 1.18; 95% CI [1.09, 1.29]; p < 0.001) demonstrated increased referral odds. Provider specialty was associated with PT referral, with non-operative sports medicine providers having the highest referral odds (OR, 3.00; 95% CI [2.72, 3.31]; p < 0.001) relative to orthopaedic surgery. CONCLUSION: Despite strong clinical practice guidelines recommending PT, formal referral rates for patients with KOA remain low regardless of insurance type, patient characteristics, and referring healthcare provider specialty. Low formal PT referral rates may represent a barrier to evidence-based KOA care.

metadata.title: Prevalence and predictors of in-class dozing among collegiate athletes and non-athletes.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adequate sleep is critical for recovery and performance, yet athletes often experience less sleep than non-athletes, potentially impacting their academic performance. This study investigates the prevalence and factors in-class dozing among collegiate athletes compared to non-athletes. METHODS: This cross-sectional study surveyed 165 athletes and 92 non-athletes using an anonymous online questionnaire, focusing on sleep duration, commute times, part-time employment, and attitudes towards sleeping in class. RESULTS: Athletes reported a higher frequency of in-class dozing (70.4%) compared to non-athletes (55.5%, P=0.009). The primary reason for in-class dozing among athletes was fatigue from sports practice, whereas non-athletes attributed it to part-time work. Logistic regression analysis revealed that athletes had a higher risk of in-class dozing (OR=2.71, 95% CI 1.42-5.16, P=0.002), and both younger age (OR=0.46, 95% CI 0.24-0.87, P=0.016) and insufficient sleep at night (OR=0.71, 95% CI 0.55-0.92, P=0.010) were associated with increased risk. CONCLUSIONS: Both athletes and non-athletes are not obtaining adequate sleep, with athletes particularly affected by training-related fatigue possibly causing in-class dozing. Factors contributing to the likelihood of in-class dozing included younger age, inadequate nightly sleep, being an athlete, and engagement in part-time employment.

metadata.title: Breast Injuries in Women's Rugby Union: A Comparison of Prospective and Retrospective Surveillance.
metadata.abstract: Retrospective research has reported a high prevalence of breast injuries in women's rugby union (RU); however, most injuries are not reported to medical staff. This study compared the incidence and severity of breast injuries collected both prospectively and retrospectively over a comparable match exposure period. Prospective surveillance was conducted by clinicians (n = 14) using an online injury surveillance system across 140 RU players. Retrospective surveillance was conducted using an anonymous online survey completed by 370 RU players. Injury incidence was calculated per 1000 hours of match exposure. Severity was assessed using breast pain, bruising and swelling, ability to continue play, perceived effect on performance, and long-term breast changes. Three breast injuries were prospectively recorded over 1204 hours of competition (2.5 injuries/1000 hours). In contrast, 144 breast injuries were reported retrospectively over 5055 hours of competition (28.5 injuries/1000 hours). The retrospective injury rate was significantly higher than the prospective rate (IRR = 11.4, 95% CI: 3.15-41.73; p < 0.002). Ninety-six percent (n = 139) of retrospectively reported injuries had not been disclosed to medical staff. Injury severity was similar between surveillance methods, with bruising commonly reported, all players continuing to participate despite injury, and over half perceiving a negative effect on performance. Long-term breast changes were reported by 6% (n = 8) of players. The substantially lower incidence recorded prospectively suggests that breast injuries are underreported in women's RU. Improved reporting and surveillance strategies are required to better capture breast injuries and support female athlete health and performance.

metadata.title: Longitudinal Serum Biomarker Profiles of Inflammation and Cartilage Matrix Metabolism During the First Year After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury initiates biological processes linked to joint tissue degeneration. The longitudinal time course of serum biomarkers reflecting inflammation and cartilage metabolism after ACL reconstruction (ACLR), particularly in comparison with uninjured controls, has not been characterized across the first postoperative year. HYPOTHESIS: Inflammatory (monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 [MCP-1]) and degradative (matrix metalloproteinase-3 [MMP-3]) biomarker concentrations would be elevated pre-ACLR and decrease over time, whereas cartilage turnover biomarker concentrations (cartilage oligomeric matrix protein [COMP] and type II collagen degradation-to-synthesis ratio [C2C:CPII]) would increase postoperatively. Also, pre-ACLR biomarker concentrations would be associated with concentrations at 6 and 12 months post-ACLR. STUDY DESIGN: Cohort study; Level of evidence, 2. METHODS: A total of 33 individuals with ACL injuries (52% female; mean age, 20.8 ± 2.4 years) were evaluated pre-ACLR and at 6 and 12 months post-ACLR. A total of 33 matched uninjured controls were included. Serum concentrations of MCP-1, MMP-3, COMP, and C2C:CPII were assessed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Linear mixed-effects models with model-based contrasts were used to evaluate differences across groups and time points. ACLR-only linear mixed-effects regression models were used to assess associations between pre-ACLR and follow-up biomarker concentrations. Exploratory post hoc models evaluated differences by concomitant injury status. RESULTS: MCP-1 was elevated in individuals with ACL injuries compared with controls at all ACLR time points (all Padj < .001), with no change across ACLR time points. MMP-3 increased from pre-ACLR to 6 months post-ACLR (Padj < .001) but did not differ from controls at any time point. COMP was consistently greater in individuals with ACL injuries than in controls at all time points (all Padj≤ .021), with no changes across ACLR time points. C2C:CPII was greater at 12 months post-ACLR than at pre-ACLR and 6 months post-ACLR (both Padj < .001) and than in uninjured controls (Padj = .001). Pre-ACLR MCP-1, MMP-3, and COMP concentrations were associated with concentrations at both 6 and 12 months post-ACLR (all P≤ .006), whereas C2C:CPII was associated only with 12-month concentrations (P = .018). CONCLUSION: Inflammatory and cartilage-related biomarkers remain altered throughout the first year after ACLR, suggesting that the biological response is not fully resolved by reconstruction and standard rehabilitation but extends beyond the early postoperative period.

metadata.title: Recovery of Pre-symptomatic Tegner Activity Level After Double-Level Osteotomy for Medial Compartment Osteoarthritis: Outcomes at 24 Months.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Double-level osteotomy (DLO) provides high return-to-sport rates, but these are generally based on the immediate preoperative activity level, which may already be reduced by knee pain. We evaluated recovery to a recalled pre-symptomatic activity level and associated factors. HYPOTHESIS: Recovery would be less frequent against the pre-symptomatic reference than the immediate preoperative level. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 51 DLO patients wishing to resume sports, with symptom durations below five years. Tegner activity scale (TAS) scores were recalled for five years before surgery and assessed immediately preoperatively and at 12 and 24 months. Exploratory Firth logistic regression included age, BMI, Kellgren-Lawrence grade, and preoperative Pain Catastrophizing Scale (PCS) to examine failure to recover the five-year TAS at 24 months. RESULTS: Median [IQR] TAS was 5 [4-8] at the five-year reference, 3 [1-5] preoperatively, 4 [2-5] at 12 months, and 4 [3-7] at 24 months. At 24 months, 56.9% recovered the five-year TAS versus 88.2% recovering the preoperative TAS. Higher PCS was associated with failure to recover the five-year TAS (adjusted OR per point, 1.066; 95% CI, 1.008-1.143; p = 0.025). DISCUSSION: Recovery proportions differed by reference, with interpretation limited by recall bias and patient selection. Higher PCS was associated with non-recovery in exploratory analysis. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III; retrospective cohort study.

metadata.title: Study of Transdermal Buprenorphine Patch versus Oral Etoricoxib for Postoperative Pain Management after Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Randomized Comparative Open-label Study.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is a widely performed procedure for end-stage knee osteoarthritis, providing significant pain relief, improved joint function, and better quality of life. However, it is associated with substantial postoperative pain, which may delay mobilization, impair rehabilitation, prolong hospital stay, and increase the risk of chronic postoperative pain, thus making effective perioperative analgesia crucial for achieving optimal postoperative outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and tolerability of transdermal buprenorphine patch versus oral etoricoxib for postoperative pain management in patients undergoing TKA, using Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores at rest and during movement for up to 1 week. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This randomized comparative study enrolled 88 patients of American Society of Anesthesiologists grade I/II after ethical approval. The patients were randomly allocated into two groups of 44 patients each. In Group A, patients received oral etoricoxib (90 mg), 1 h before surgery with a sip of water, and in Group B, patients received a transdermal buprenorphine patch (10 µg/h), 12 h before surgery. For statistical analysis, the Chi-square test and Student's t-test were used. RESULTS: Statistically significant differences were observed in VAS scores (at rest and during movement), with Group B demonstrating significantly lower pain. Furthermore, rescue analgesic requirements and length of hospital stay were reduced significantly in Group B, thus indicating overall superior postoperative pain control. CONCLUSION: Transdermal buprenorphine patch offers sustained analgesia (reduced VAS scores) with the potential for fewer systemic side effects, reduced need for additional opioid and rescue analgesic requirements, leading to shorter length of hospital stay.

metadata.title: Efficacy of Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Sampling in Muscle Tears and Intersex Differences in Professional Football Players: A Cohort Study.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the gold standard for monitoring the evolution of muscle injuries in athletes, although no established quantitative measure of recovery currently exists. HYPOTHESIS: Apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values may provide a quantitative measure of muscle healing, and sex-related differences may exist in the evolution of muscle injuries. STUDY DESIGN: Single-center retrospective observational cohort study. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 2a. METHODS: Twenty-six professional football (soccer) players (13 male ,13 female) undergoing MRI for muscle injury were retrospectively selected between October 2020 and June 2024. All athletes underwent MRI at baseline (T0) and at 2-week follow-up, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) acquisitions with b values of 0-100-800 s/mm². Two musculoskeletal radiologists measured ADC values within the index lesions at each examination. Changes in ADC between the two time points (ΔADC) were assessed using a paired-samples t test, while sex-related differences were evaluated using the Mann-Whitney U test. RESULTS: The overall mean ADC value at the lesion site decreased from 2.06 ± 0.35 mm2/s at T0 to 1.61 ± 0.30 mm2/s at follow-up corresponding to a mean ΔADC of 0.44 ± 0.20 and a 21.84% reduction. The difference between T0 and follow-up was statistically significant (t = 8.12; P < 0.001). Mean ΔADC values were 0.32 ± 0.20 mm²/s in male players and 0.56 ± 0.25 mm²/s in female players, respectively, with a statistically significant difference between sexes (z = -2.95; P = 0.003). When only hamstring injuries were considered, female players showed a significantly greater decrease in ADC over time than male players (Mann-Whitney U test; exact P = 0.02), with mean ΔADC values of 0.56 ± 0.30 and 0.26 ± 0.08 mm²/s, respectively. CONCLUSION: Muscle injury is associated with an acute increase in ADC values followed by a progressive decrease during healing. ADC may therefore represent a quantitative imaging biomarker for monitoring muscle recovery. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: ADC measurement within muscle tears may provide a quantitative assessment of healing status and support individualized rehabilitation strategies in athletes. Sex-related differences may exist in injury pathophysiology and recovery patterns relevant to safe return to play.

metadata.title: Athletes and Medical Staff in Elite Contact Sports: a Quantitative Analysis of Use, Knowledge, and Attitudes Regarding Cannabinoids.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cannabis use among elite contact sport athletes increases with legal reform and commercial availability. Limited education in cannabinoid pharmacology, use, and risk persists among athletes and medical staff, fostering stigma and reducing evidence-based guidance and communication. HYPOTHESIS: Athletes use cannabis but perceive stigma and discomfort discussing cannabis with medical staff. STUDY DESIGN: Quantitative, descriptive cross-sectional surveys. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4. METHODS: Two anonymous online surveys were administered to elite and professional contact sport athletes (Canada, United States, Australia) and medical and training staff (February 2023 to July 2024). Descriptive statistics assessed demographics, use patterns, knowledge, education needs, attitudes, stigma, communication, and league policies. RESULTS: A total of 166 athletes (89.7% male, 35.2% aged 18-23 years) and 64 medical staff (physicians, athletic therapists, strength and conditioning coaches, etc) responded. Knowledge (pharmacology, interactions, dosing) was low. Overall, 56% of athletes currently used cannabinoids (81% having ever used), but only 21.7% knew the endocannabinoid system and 67.4% were unfamiliar with therapeutic dosing. Among medical staff, 59.5% were unfamiliar with mechanisms, only 14% were familiar with dosing protocols, and 71.4% lacked confidence in making treatment plans. Of the athletes, 86.5% believed cannabis had therapeutic value, 72.3% wanted education, and 74.1% favored qualified scientists as instructors. Of the medical staff, 79.5% reported strong educational need, with 100% of staff desiring athlete-specific cannabinoid education. Stigma and communication barriers were substantial: 81.3% of athletes perceived public stigma, 66.1% perceived staff stigma, and only 21.4% felt comfortable discussing cannabis with medical staff. Staff believed athletes would be honest if approached; however, <50% believed athletes trusted them enough to start the conversation. Both athletes and medical staff categorized cannabinoids as supplements or medications (unlike street drugs) and both supported legalization and a revision and update on league cannabis policies. CONCLUSION: Athletes and medical staff exhibit parallel knowledge gaps and strong educational needs amid high interest, use, and significant communication barriers. Evidence-informed education and stigma-reducing strategies are urgently needed. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Athletes increasingly use cannabinoids for pain, sleep, and recovery, while medical staff report insufficient training and low confidence. System-level education, communication, and policy updates may improve safety, decision-making, and trust.

metadata.title: Warning signs of Injury: Changes in pain, training load, and wellness in elite youth athletes.
metadata.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Examine week-by-week changes during the four weeks preceding injury compared with injury-free weeks. DESIGN: Prospective study. SETTING: and main outcome: Training load was calculated as (weekly training minutes x average weekly rate of perceived exertion)/1000 (sRPE). Pain was assessed with a rating scale 0-10. Wellness (sleep, fatigue, stress and mental recovery) were standardized using Z-scores. Injury was self-reported. PARTICIPANTS: Elite youth athletes. RESULTS: Among 146 athletes, 118 (80.8%) reported 125 injuries. Mean age was 17.0 (SD 0.8). Compared with injury-free weeks, significantly higher pain scores were observed one (md [IQR]: 2.0 [0.0-4.0], p = 0.039) and two weeks (2.0 [1.0-3.0], p = 0.047) prior to injury. Median sRPE was significantly lower three (md [IQR]: 2.30 [0.75-4.20], p = 0.012) and four weeks (2.40 [0.96-3.96], p = 0.011). Sleep, stress and total wellness were significantly lower one week (mean [SD]: -0.348 [1.1], p = 0.004; -0.272 [0.9], p = 0.017; -0.244 [1.0], p = 0.011), while stress also showed reduction two weeks prior to injury (-0.244 [1.0], p = 0.042). CONCLUSION: Changes were observed mainly in the week preceding injury. Increased pain and reduced wellness may serve as early warning signs, while decreased training load may reflect adaptation rather than causation. These findings support injury as a progressive process with detectable warning signs.

metadata.title: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome in Athletes: A Narrative Review of Diagnostic Challenges, Management Strategies, and Return-to-Play Outcomes.
metadata.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Thoracic outlet syndrome (TOS) is a compression disorder involving the brachial plexus, subclavian artery, or subclavian vein within the thoracic outlet. Athletes represent a distinct population in whom delayed diagnosis may result in career-threatening injuries. OBJECTIVES: This review aimed to: (i) identify diagnostic pitfalls in athletes not captured by conventional provocative tests; (ii) evaluate conservative and operative management by TOS subtype; (iii) synthesize return-to-play (RTP) rates, timelines, and clearance criteria; and (iv) highlight methodological limitations and propose minimum reporting standards for future athlete-specific studies. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to July 2026 using controlled vocabulary and free-text terms for TOS, its subtypes, Paget-Schroetter syndrome, and athletic populations. Reference lists were hand-searched. Studies addressing TOS diagnosis, classification, pathophysiology, management, or RTP in athletes were eligible regardless of design, reflecting limited randomized evidence. Journal legitimacy was screened using the Kscien's list. RESULTS: nTOS is the predominant form in athletes and usually improves with 4-6 months of rehabilitation, whereas refractory cases may require surgery. vTOS/Paget-Schroetter syndrome requires urgent thrombolysis and early first-rib resection; aTOS is rare but limb-threatening and requires prompt surgery. Mixed presentations occur in up to 23% of surgical cases. CONCLUSIONS: Outcomes are favorable with subtype-specific diagnosis and objective RTP criteria. However, evidence is limited by retrospective, single-center studies with pooled subtypes, inconsistent RTP definitions, and selective reporting. Prospective, sport-specific studies using standardized outcomes are needed.

metadata.title: Developmental Differences in Muscle, Tendon, and Cartilage Injuries in Elite Badminton.
metadata.abstract: This study investigated severe muscle, tendon, and cartilage injury characteristics by injury timing and post-injury management among elite badminton players. A retrospective interview study was conducted with 126 badminton players aged 19-24 years. A total of 87 severe injury cases reported by 73 athletes were analyzed, with some athletes contributing more than one case. Injuries were classified by timing into the secondary school group (SSG, n = 33) and the post-secondary group (PSG, n = 54). Injury characteristics and post-injury management were compared using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, with effect sizes. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) examined associations with injury timing. Compared with the SSG, the PSG had higher odds of lower limb muscle injuries (OR = 6.00, 95% CI = 1.85-19.47, p = .003) and smash/stroke-related injuries (OR = 5.43, 95% CI = 1.15-25.66, p = .033), whereas the PSG had lower odds of lower limb tendinopathies (OR = 0.21, 95% CI = 0.08-0.55, p = .001). These findings suggest that severe injury characteristics may differ according to the timing of injury occurrence, despite no significant between-group differences in post-injury management, and may help inform potential injury prevention priorities based on the observed injury patterns.

metadata.title: A practical pipeline for patient-specific musculoskeletal modeling: a comprehensive MRI-based framework.
metadata.abstract: Patient-specific musculoskeletal (MS) modeling can provide estimates of internal joint loading that canot be measured directly. However, limitations in automated segmentation due to data-scarce environments, morphing difficulty caused by anatomical variability, and functional nonalignment are major bottlenecks that hinder the practical application of modeling and reduce productivity in MS research. To comprehensively address these practical issues, this study proposes and validates an integrated, automated modeling framework. First, we automatically segmented the lower extremity bones of the 4 knee osteoarthritis patients using a multi-atlas-based segmentation algorithm. By integrating the segmented bone with motion capture and force plate data, a modeling pipeline including multi-stage morphing and functional alignment processes was implemented. Using the constructed customized model, the medial and lateral knee contact forces (FMCandFLC) were estimated during a single-leg step-up exercise, and these were compared and evaluated against the results based on manual segmentation. The contact forces estimated through the automated segmentation framework demonstrated high consistency with the manual results. The mean absolute error ranged from 0.04 ± 0.03-0.06 ± 0.03 BW forFMC, and from 0.06 ± 0.04-0.09 ± 0.07 BW forFLC, and the intraclass correlation coefficient demonstrated a high correlation of over 0.99 across all patients. This study demonstrated that the proposed automated pipeline provides a practical approach to address misalignment caused by anatomical variability, while generating joint load estimates equivalent to the manual approach. By addressing key methodological challenges, this study will bring patient-specific models closer to future clinical application, where they could help assess individual loading across different activities and inform treatment and rehabilitation strategies.

metadata.title: Long-Term Failure Rate of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Using All-Inside 4-Stranded Semitendinosus Autograft Is 20.5.
metadata.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate outcomes (graft failure, Patient-Reported Outcome Measures, and knee stability) after primary isolated anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction using the all-inside technique with 4-stranded semitendinosus autograft fixed between 2 adjustable-loop cortical suspension devices, with a minimum follow-up of 10 years. METHODS: Patients who underwent primary isolated ACL reconstruction using the all-inside 4-stranded semitendinosus between January 2011 and January 2013, with a minimum of 10-year follow-up, were included. Patients completed a standardized questionnaire and were offered a follow-up consultation. The questionnaire included the Tegner, ACL-Return to Sport after Injury, Subjective Knee Value, subjective International Knee Documentation Committee, and assessment of graft failure. Clinical evaluations and laxity measurements were conducted during follow-up consultations. RESULTS: At a mean follow-up of 138 months (range: 122-159), 156 patients completed the questionnaire, and 111 were clinically evaluated. The mean age was 39.6 ± 9.7 years (range: 15-62). Graft failure occurred in 20.5% of cases (32/156). The mean decrease in Tegner was 1.03 ± 1.23 points, and 51% returned to their preinjury sport level. The median preoperative Tegner was 7.0 (interquartile range: 6.0-7.0). A higher preoperative Tegner was associated with an increased risk of graft failure (P = .016). Graft failure occurred in 23% of males and 16.6% of females (P = .461). Patients with grafts sized ≤8 mm (n = 85) had a failure rate of 17.5%, compared with 23.9% for grafts >8 mm (P = .441). The mean subjective International Knee Documentation Committee was 85.6 ± 13.5, Subjective Knee Value 79.2 ± 22.1, and ACL-Return to Sport after Injury 69.5 ± 26.5. Among patients without reported graft failure, 16.5% exhibited >3 mm differential anterior laxity, and 28% had a pivot-shift score ≥2. CONCLUSIONS: At a minimum 10-year follow-up, primary isolated ACL reconstruction using an all-inside 4-stranded semitendinosus autograft showed a 20.5% graft failure rate, despite favorable patient-reported outcomes. A higher preoperative Tegner showed a trend toward increased graft failure. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, retrospective case series.

metadata.title: Bone Mineral Density in Physique-Focused and Non-Physique-Focused Female Collegiate Athletes: Associations With Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport Risk Factors.
metadata.abstract: Kolb, DE, Cipriano, NL, Moody, RA, Stephens, JA, Caldwell, LK, Lindley, MR, Ware, ME, and Deemer, SE. Bone mineral density in physique-focused and non-physique-focused female collegiate athletes: Associations with relative energy deficiency in sport risk factors. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-Bone mineral density (BMD) is a critical indicator of skeletal health and long-term injury risk in athletic populations. Female athletes are susceptible to changes in BMD because of sport-specific training demands, hormonal dysregulation, and energy availability. The present study aimed to compare BMD between physique-focused (PF; endurance, aesthetic, and weight-dependent sports) and non-physique-focused (NPF; ball, power, and skill-based sports) female collegiate athletes and assess risk factors associated with relative energy deficiency in sport (REDs) across both groups. Thirty-three female athletes were evaluated for BMD by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), REDs risk using the Clinical Assessment Tool 2 (CAT2), anthropometric measurements, blood biomarkers, the Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire (EDE-Q), and the Low Energy Availability in Females Questionnaire (LEAF-Q). Group differences were assessed using independent t-tests with significance set at p < 0.05. Physique-focused athletes demonstrated significantly lower DXA-derived z-scores at anteroposterior spine, right and left femur, and total body sites than NPF athletes (p < 0.001). There were no differences in leptin (p = 0.35), cortisol (p = 0.16), vitamin D (p = 0.29), LEAF-Q total score (p = 0.72), or global EDE-Q score (p = 0.10). No group differences in CAT2 REDs risk were observed; thus, subjects were combined: 19 athletes were classified as "green;" 12 were "yellow;" and 2 were "orange." Lower BMD in PF athletes supports the importance of early screening and targeted interventions to support bone health. These findings suggest sport type may influence skeletal outcomes independent of traditional REDs indicators, emphasizing the need for sport-specific assessment strategies.

metadata.title: Advanced Analytics Show Domain-Specific Performance Changes After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction in National Football League Players.
metadata.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate return to play, performance, and assess performance changes after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction using advanced statistics in National Football League players. METHODS: National Football League players who underwent anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) between 2017 and 2024 were identified using publicly available databases and injury reports. Demographic and outcome data for 1 year preinjury to 2 years postinjury were obtained. Return to play was defined as being listed as active for a regular season game after injury. Return to performance was defined as returning to greater than 90% of preinjury performance. Our primary performance outcome was Sports Information Solutions points above replacement (PAR). Binary logistic regression was used to determine factors associated with return to play and return to performance. Preinjury and postinjury performance data at the first and second postinjury year were compared with paired t-tests. RESULTS: We included 237 players in return-to-play and 173 players in return-to-performance analyses. Of players, 75.5% returned to play; players with more preinjury games played, more index games played, starters, and players with greater preinjury PAR were more likely to return to play (P = .03, P < .001, P < .001, P < .001, respectively). Fifty-one percent of players who returned to play returned to performance; younger age and players with lower preinjury PAR were significantly more likely to return to performance (P = .004, P < .001). Total PAR was significantly decreased at the postinjury year 1 and year 2 seasons (P = .002, P = .004), driven at both time points by significantly decreased rushing (P = .02, P = .001) and pass coverage (P = .003, P = .03) PAR. CONCLUSIONS: After anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, National Football League players with more preinjury games played and higher preinjury performance are more likely to return to play; younger players with lower preinjury performance are more likely to return to performance; and there is a significant decrease in overall performance 1 and 2 years after injury, driven by decreased rushing and pass coverage performance. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, retrospective case series.

metadata.title: Do Athletes Lose Soleus Strength Over the Course of a Season? Longitudinal Monitoring of Seated Plantar Flexion Maximum Voluntary Contraction Strength and Factors That Affect It in Australian Football Players.
metadata.abstract: Green, B, Pizzari, T, Schache, AG, Rio, EK, Evans, SCS, Cooper, S, and Murphy, MC. Do athletes lose soleus strength over the course of a season? Longitudinal monitoring of seated plantar flexion maximum voluntary contraction strength and factors that affect it in Australian football players. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The calf muscles are critical to dynamic lower-limb function in sports but are susceptible to injury. Despite its role in performance and injury, research has not evaluated soleus strength changes over the course of a season, or factors affecting it. Flexed-knee maximum plantar flexion strength was longitudinally monitored in state-league Australian footballers (2 Western Australian and 1 Victorian team) across 1-season at timepoints: preseason (T0), early in-season (T1), late in-season (T2). Generalized estimating equations evaluated strength outcomes over time (absolute, relative, asymmetry). Intrinsic factors (e.g., age, sex, injury history, sport exposure history, calf-focused resistance training) were analyzed to determine longitudinal associations with strength. Forty-one athletes (32 male, 9 female) were monitored across 210 strength measurements from T0 to T2. Absolute (T0 = 121.7 ± 27 kg; T1 = 135.2 ± 27.3 kg; T2 = 135.8 ± 25.9 kg) and relative (T0 = 1.51 ± 0.28 body mass [BM]; T1 = 1.69 ± 0.27 BM, T2 = 1.75 ± 0.26 BM) strength demonstrated longitudinal change (absolute: β = 19.33 kg, relative: β = 0.24 BM; p < 0.001). Reduced strength was associated with a recent calf injury history (relative and absolute: p < 0.001) and older age (p = 0.03). Lower strength (absolute: β = -23.53 kg, relative: β = -0.22 BM; p < 0.05) and larger asymmetry (β = 8.13 kg, p = 0.01) were detected in female athletes. Athletes can be expected to improve and maintain soleus capacity across seasonal periods. Athlete age, calf injury history, and sex can affect strength longitudinally. These findings may guide individualized prevention, performance, and postinjury benchmarking.

metadata.title: Conductive Composite-Based Wearable Sensors for Sports Science: Intelligent Data Analysis and Emerging Applications.
metadata.abstract: Wearable sensors enable continuous acquisition of physiological, biochemical, and biomechanical signals during exercise, providing data to support sports performance assessment, training regulation, fatigue monitoring, and rehabilitation interventions. However, signal reliability and multidimensional data analysis under complex motion conditions remain constrained by device functionality. Conductive composites can improve sensor flexibility, interfacial conformability, and signal acquisition performance, while artificial intelligence (AI) enables movement pattern recognition, state assessment, and outcome prediction from complex data. Their integration is advancing wearable systems toward multimodal sensing and intelligent analysis. Guided by application needs in sports, this review summarizes emerging applications of wearable sensing technologies enabled by conductive composites and AI. First, the relevance to sports science and the data characteristics of physiological, biochemical, and biomechanical signals are introduced. The functional characteristics, representative applications, and major limitations of conductive polymer, carbon-based, MXene, and hydrogel composites are then summarized. Regarding algorithms, the fundamental principles of supervised learning, unsupervised learning, deep learning (DL), and large language models (LLMs) are discussed, with comparisons of their capabilities in feature extraction, temporal modeling, and multisource data analysis, as well as their input data requirements. On this basis, advances in the application of these systems to sports performance and sport-specific movement monitoring, exercise-induced fatigue monitoring and assessment, sports injury identification and evaluation, and intelligent monitoring of sports rehabilitation are reviewed followed by a discussion of current challenges and future directions. Through the coordinated integration of material design, signal acquisition, and intelligent analysis, wearable systems are expected to enable continuous, reliable, and individualized assessment of exercise-related states, with further applications in real-time feedback, risk alerts, and training decision support, providing a technological foundation for scientifically informed training, sports rehabilitation, and individual health management.

metadata.title: Repeated sprint training in hypoxia as a post-surgical rehabilitation strategy: A case study in an elite badminton player.
metadata.abstract: Badminton is a racquet sport that imposes high demands on both aerobic and anaerobic capacity and involves repetitive, high-intensity movements, increasing the risk of non-contact injuries to joints and muscle-tendon units. Returning to sport-specific conditioning after injury, particularly post-surgery, presents challenges for deconditioned athletes seeking to restore aerobic capacity while minimising mechanical stress imposed on the injured parts. This case study evaluated the feasibility of integrating short-term repeated sprint training in hypoxia (RSH) as a supplementary modality within a late-stage post-lower back surgery rehabilitation program to support aerobic reconditioning before return to sport-specific conditioning. An elite men's singles badminton athlete completed 4-week RSH (FiO2 ~ 16.5%), alongside his regular rehabilitation schedule. The intervention consisted of 20 × 4-s all-out cycling sprints interspersed with 30-56-s recovery, performed once weekly. Post-intervention lactate profiling suggested a rightward shift in the blood lactate curve, with estimated increases of 33% and 10% in power output at the aerobic and anaerobic thresholds, respectively, indicative of aerobic reconditioning. However, the present findings should be interpreted cautiously due to observed stage-to-stage blood lactate variability, single-case design, and concurrent rehabilitation. Overall, the present study supports the feasibility of incorporating hypoxic RSH in late-stage rehabilitation to facilitate return to sport-specific conditioning.

metadata.title: Quadriceps Strength After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: Mechanisms of Weakness and Evidence-Based Rehabilitation Strategies.
metadata.abstract: Impairment of quadriceps strength is a frequent and clinically important problem after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury and reconstruction. This dysfunction reflects muscular, neural, surgical, and rehabilitation-related mechanisms and is not solely attributable to muscle atrophy. Despite restoration of joint stability, quadriceps weakness can persist and contribute to delayed functional recovery and reduced readiness to return to sport. A comprehensive assessment should integrate clinical examination, objective isometric or isokinetic strength testing, rate of force development, functional performance, quality of movement, imaging investigations, and patient-reported and psychological measures. Rehabilitation should be initiated preoperatively and continue postoperatively with a focus on control of effusion and restoration of extension, early quadriceps activation, progressive resistance exercise, appropriate open-chain loading followed by eccentric, plyometric, and sport-specific training. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation has supportive evidence as an adjunct, and blood-flow restriction training may be useful when higher loads may not yet be tolerated. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the mechanisms and rehabilitation of quadriceps weakness after ACL injury and ACL reconstruction, highlighting clinically relevant strategies for restoring strength and neuromuscular function.

metadata.title: Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport and its Implications for the Foot and Ankle Surgeon.
metadata.abstract: Relative energy deficiency in sport (RED-S) is a syndrome caused by low energy availability that affects multiple physiologic systems in both male and female athletes. Stress fractures of the foot and ankle are often the first signs of RED-S; therefore, it is crucial that orthopedic surgeons are aware of and able to identify this disorder. This article focuses on RED-S and provides a framework for understanding the disorder, it's relevancy to the orthopedic foot and ankle surgeon, and offers suggestions for diagnostic strategies and treatment approaches that are imperative for safe return to play.

metadata.title: Editorial Commentary: Allograft Reconstruction in Chronic Proximal Hamstring Tendon Avulsions: Bridging the Gap May Not Equal a Full Return.
metadata.abstract: Proximal hamstring tendon avulsions are being treated surgically at rising rates, and although primary repair reliably restores function and return to sport in the acute setting, chronic and significantly retracted tears present a far more difficult problem. When direct repair is not feasible for a chronic, retracted proximal hamstring tendon avulsion, allograft reconstruction offers a bridge across a gap that would otherwise go unaddressed. However, significant chronicity and retraction are difficult challenges to overcome, and patient expectations must be appropriately counseled. As a salvage procedure, allograft reconstruction may improve patient outcomes significantly; however, it is not expected to restore full function, return athletic individuals to their baseline and preinjury level of sports participation, or match the success of primary repair. Allograft reconstruction may also carry more than double the risk of rerupture, which is important to discuss with patients up front. Graft choice and postoperative rehabilitation protocols remain heterogeneous across the limited available literature, and a validated tool to risk-stratify which chronic, retracted tears are best served by reconstruction versus continued nonoperative management does not yet exist. These findings suggest that allograft reconstruction is a viable and clinically meaningful option for a difficult, often nonoperatively unsalvageable problem, but surgeons should frame it for patients as a salvage procedure rather than a full restoration of function, and expectations should be set accordingly.

metadata.title: Medical resource use by Team USA at the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games: an observational study.
metadata.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To quantify medical resource utilisation among Team USA during the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games, by illness and injury status. METHODS: This was an epidemiological study of athletes who sought care in the medical clinics in the Athlete Village (n=206). Athletes were categorised as those who incurred injury (INJ; n=77), who incurred physical or mental illness (ILL; n=53) and who had no health concerns (NHC; n=76). The NHC group sought maintenance, recovery and mental performance services. Clinic encounters, encounter time, medical providers and service types accessed (therapy, procedures, pharmacological treatment, diagnostics, advanced imaging) were collected during 26 January-25 February 2026. RESULTS: 1702 clinical encounters were documented. INJ, ILL and had greater clinic visit numbers per athlete (9.6±7.7, 8.5±8.6 and 7.4±7.2 visits, respectively; p=0.049), with maintenance/massage accounting for most encounters. INJ demonstrated the greatest healthcare needs, with longer clinic time per athlete (5.1±4.2 hours vs 4.3±4.3 hours and 3.8±3.4 hours, respectively; p=0.029), accession of more medical staff provider types, particularly physicians and chiropractors (3.1 provider types vs 2.3 and 1.8 provider types; p<0.001), more procedures and more hospital visits. ILL had the highest use of diagnostic testing and pharmacological interventions (p<0.001). Therapy-based services were used by 87%-100% of all groups. Massage was included in 62%, 66% and 67% of maintenance visits for INJ, ILL and NHC, respectively. Similar proportions of all three groups sought care from athletic trainers (42.0%-58.4%), physical therapists (28.9%-34%), massage therapists (55.3%-66.0%) and psychological service providers (9.2%-24.0%). CONCLUSION: Medical resource use in this game predominantly involved delivering care to athletes for non-injury/illness reasons. Therefore, it is important to bring healthcare staff with specialised skills in complementary medicine, recovery, mental well-being and performance domains to address needs along the healthcare spectrum.
