metadata.title: Flexible and stretchable bioelectronics for sports wearable monitoring: Materials, Device Engineering, and Intelligent Wearable Platforms.
metadata.abstract: Modern sports science is undergoing a paradigm shift from subjective coaching to objective, data-driven precision training. Consequently, wearable electronics for acquiring precise data during sports activities are attracting attention. However, conventional rigid wearables inherently suffer from mechanical mismatches between rigid wearables and the soft, deformable human skin, inducing severe motion artifacts and restricting natural biomechanics during high-intensity athletic activities. To address these limitations from a comprehensive perspective, this review systematically summarizes and analyzes recent advancements in next-generation flexible and stretchable bioelectronics tailored specifically for sports applications. We systematically examine the substrate materials, structural engineering designs, and device-level optimization strategies required to withstand repetitive strain, shear, and sweat-intensive environments. Building upon these conformable bio-interfaces, we discuss three core sensing modalities: electrochemical sensors for real-time analysis of sweat biomarkers, biophysical sensors for continuous electrophysiological and hemodynamic monitoring, and electromechanical sensors for high-fidelity kinematic and impact tracking. Furthermore, we discuss body-derived energy harvesting strategies to power sports wearables and wireless communication systems for continuous athletic monitoring. The importance of artificial intelligence and machine learning is increasing, as these techniques enable the removal of motion artifacts and facilitate objective analysis of athletic data for training and health monitoring applications. By evaluating targeted applications across aerobic and anaerobic exercise, cognitive state assessment, and post-exercise recovery, this review demonstrates how next-generation sports wearables contribute to the shift in sports science from reactive treatment toward proactive, data-driven performance enhancement and injury prevention.

metadata.title: Limb Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Rats is partially mediated by enhancing Necroptosis via Phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL.
metadata.abstract: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury (L-IRI) causes severe skeletal muscle damage and functional impairment through activation of regulated cell-death and inflammatory pathways. Necroptosis is a regulated form of necrotic cell death mediated through the receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)-RIPK3-mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) signaling axis. Prior experimental studies have shown that Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1) attenuates acute skeletal muscle ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats. However, how Nec-1-sensitive protection relates to RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, circulating muscle injury markers, inflammatory responses, histological damage, and functional recovery during the early postischemic period remains incompletely defined. In this study, we used a rat model of unilateral hindlimb ischemia involving 3 hours of ischemia followed by reperfusion for up to 7 days to evaluate these interrelated responses. Nec-1 was administered before ischemia and after reperfusion. L-IRI resulted in elevated plasma creatine kinase and lactate dehydrogenase levels, severe histopathological injury, increased TUNEL staining, impaired grip strength, and reduced Modified Tarlov scores. These changes were accompanied by increased phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL, activation of inflammatory signaling pathways, and altered expression of injury-associated inflammatory mediators. Nec-1 treatment reduced RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, inflammatory mediator expression, circulating muscle injury markers, and histological injury while preserving muscle architecture and improving functional recovery. These findings support and extend previous evidence that Nec-1-sensitive necroptosis-associated signaling contributes to early skeletal muscle injury following L-IRI. Pharmacologic targeting of regulated necrotic and inflammatory pathways warrants further investigation as a potential adjunct strategy for limiting acute skeletal muscle injury after limb reperfusion.

metadata.title: Pre-season friendly match-play as a double-edged sword: Performance gains and inflammatory cost in semi-professional soccer players (a natural experiment).
metadata.abstract: Pre-season training prepares soccer players for competition, but the longitudinal effects of friendly match exposure remain unclear. We investigated whether cumulative late pre-season match-play is associated with physiological adaptation in semi-professional players. Twenty-four male players from a randomly selected semi-professional team competing at national level were assessed at pre-season start, mid-pre-season and pre-competition. Measurements included body composition, physical performance, aerobic fitness and blood markers reflecting muscle damage, inflammation, hormonal status and haematological adaptation. Based on cumulative playing time across eight friendly matches, as determined by coaching staff, players were classified retrospectively into extended play (EP) or limited play (LP) groups. Controlling for mid-pre-season baseline, the EP group showed significantly lower pre-competition values for body mass ( η p 2 = 0.276), body fat ( η p 2 = 0.294) and 35 m sprint time ( η p 2 = 0.129) and higher values for lower-limb power (dominant/non-dominant; η p 2 = 0.219-0.424), velocity at maximal oxygen uptake ( η p 2 = 0.441) and at second ventilatory threshold ( η p 2 = 0.708), serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase ( η p 2 = 0.296), myoglobin ( η p 2 = 0.199), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein ( η p 2 = 0.920), interleukin-6 ( η p 2 = 0.893), tumour necrosis factor-α ( η p 2 = 0.937) and red blood cell count ( η p 2 = 0.190) (all P ≤ 0.038). Across all participants, total match-play time was correlated significantly with reductions in body fat (r = -0.47) and increases in lower-limb power (r = 0.44-0.67), second ventilatory threshold (r = 0.55) and inflammatory markers (r = 0.79-0.86) (all P ≤ 0.033). Greater friendly match-play exposure during pre-season was associated with favourable physiological adaptations and a more pronounced physiological and inflammatory response. These findings support friendly match-play as a meaningful physiological stimulus and highlight the importance of balancing match exposure with recovery during pre-season preparation.

metadata.title: Selective Electrical Muscle Stimulation of the Vastus Medialis in a Patient With Knee Osteoarthritis, With Changes in Muscle Quality, Symptoms, and Physical Activity: A Case Report.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND Fat accumulation in the vastus medialis has been associated with the progression of knee osteoarthritis. Electrical muscle stimulation may reduce intramuscular fat accumulation by inducing contractions of the targeted muscle. We hypothesized that electrical stimulation of the vastus medialis would be associated with a reduction in intramuscular fat and improvement in self-reported symptoms during the observation period in a patient with knee osteoarthritis. CASE REPORT The patient was a 77-year-old man with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2 right knee osteoarthritis. Because he also had hypertension and hyperlipidemia, he had maintained regular exercise habits, including aquatic walking; however, he discontinued these activities because of knee pain. Electrical stimulation was applied to the vastus medialis for 30 minutes per session, 3 times per week, for 4 weeks. Ultrasound echo intensity, an indirect indicator of intramuscular fat, and the Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score were assessed before and after the intervention. Compared with the pre-intervention value, vastus medialis echo intensity decreased by 13.7 arbitrary units (25.3%), and knee symptoms improved during the observation period. He resumed aquatic walking 2 weeks after electrical stimulation was initiated. CONCLUSIONS During the observation period, vastus medialis echo intensity decreased, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score scores improved, and he resumed aquatic walking. However, because this was a single uncontrolled case and physical activity resumed during the intervention, these changes cannot be attributed to electrical stimulation alone; spontaneous improvement, behavioral reactivation, or a combination of these factors remain plausible. Controlled studies across different levels of disease severity are needed.

metadata.title: The "Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability Technique" (MERI Technique): A Simple Lateral Tenodesis Reconstructing the Condylar Strap, the Distal Kaplan Fibers, and the Femoral Insertion of the Anterolateral Ligament to Control Internal Rotation During Anterior Cruciate Ligament Surgery.
metadata.abstract: The Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability technique is a simple and minimally invasive lateral tenodesis designed to enhance internal rotation control during anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction by reconstructing the distal Kaplan fibers, the condylar strap, and the femoral insertion of the anterolateral ligament. Using a 1-cm-wide fascia lata strip, the procedure involves fixation with a single anchor at an isometric point proximal to the anterolateral ligament insertion, followed by a continuous locking suture and fascia lata closure on the anchor, which further reinforces rotational stability without excessive constraint. Although possibly biomechanically less restrictive than traditional lateral extra-articular tenodesis, the Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability technique strikes a balance between stability and flexibility, potentially reducing postoperative stiffness and morbidity. Its simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and minimal invasiveness make it a valuable alternative for addressing anterolateral instability in select anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction patients.

metadata.title: Tunable Polycaprolactone-Gelatin Methacryloyl Composites for Fused Deposition Modeling Musculoskeletal Scaffold Fabrication.
metadata.abstract: The global musculoskeletal burden continues to outpace standard of care transplantation efforts and existing tissue engineering solutions, necessitating further development of scalable biomaterials. In this study, we introduce a novel synthesis of polycaprolactone-gelatin methacryloyl (PCL-GelMA) composite filament, compatible with standard fused deposition modeling (FDM) 3D printers, for scalable and customizable scaffold fabrication. By incorporating 15% and 30% (w/w) GelMA into a PCL matrix, we achieved tunable modulation of surface roughness, hydrophilicity, and degradation kinetics. Mechanical testing revealed nonlinear dependencies between GelMA content and tensile properties, suggesting that variation in GelMA particle size and distribution leads to a concentration-dependent trade-off between stiffness and structural integrity. Human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) cultured on printed scaffolds maintained viability and proliferative capacity. By mitigating solvent toxicity through upstream processing, physically integrating constituents into a unified bulk matrix, and leveraging the accessibility of FDM printing, this material platform enables scalable translation and further biomaterial exploration.

metadata.title: Tissue-Specific Regulation of Glucose and Lipid Metabolism by miR-29a in Insulin Resistance and Type 2 Diabetes.
metadata.abstract: MicroRNA-29a (miR-29a) has emerged as a context-dependent regulator of glucose and lipid metabolism in insulin-sensitive tissues, yet its tissue-specific actions in insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes remain incompletely understood. We synthesized peer-reviewed evidence retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCOhost on the role of miR-29a across skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, liver, and pancreatic β-cells. We first define the nomenclature and genomic organization of the miR-29 family, its upstream transcriptional regulators, and the Argonaute-based evidence that separates direct target repression from correlative association. Across these tissues, miR-29a modulates oxidative metabolism, inflammatory signaling, and mitochondrial adaptation, largely through the PPARδ/PGC-1α axis, exerting complex and sometimes opposing effects depending on the tissue environment. We further examine miR-29a as a mediator of interorgan communication through extracellular vesicles, its responsiveness to exercise, and its emerging value as a biomarker and therapeutic target, while highlighting unresolved contradictions and translational hurdles. Because miR-29 family members act as tumor suppressors in most epithelial tissues, we also address the oncogenic risk inherent in nucleic acid strategies that lower miR-29a levels. Collectively, this mini-review positions miR-29a as a physiology-oriented integrator of metabolic remodeling and tissue-specific adaptation in metabolic disease.

metadata.title: Epigallocatechin-3-gallate attenuates PAR-2-mediated inflammatory signaling and preserves markers of mitochondrial integrity in osteoarthritic chondrocytes.
metadata.abstract: Epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG), the principal catechin of green tea, exhibits broad anti-inflammatory properties; however, its effect on protease-activated receptor-2 (PAR-2)-mediated signaling in osteoarthritis (OA) has not been investigated. Here, we report that EGCG (5-10 µM) dose-dependently suppresses PAR-2 expression at both mRNA and protein levels in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated human chondrocytes derived from bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. This upstream inhibition attenuated ERK1/2 phosphorylation (pERK/total ERK ratio reduced below basal levels at 10 µM) and produced concordant suppression of three functionally linked effector arms: (i) pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, MCP-1), with near-maximal inhibition at 10 µM and a saturation plateau at 20 µM; (ii) the SOX4-ADAMTS-5 catabolic axis (81.9% and 66.2% protein reduction, respectively); and (iii) RANK/RANKL surface expression. EGCG also restored mitochondrial membrane potential and biomass to near-homeostatic levels. Crucially, small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated PAR-2 silencing reduced LPS-induced TNF-α by ~38% and substantially blunted EGCG's incremental efficacy, supporting PAR-2 as a predominant, though not exclusive, mediator of EGCG's anti-inflammatory action. The effective concentrations employed are physiologically attainable through dietary green tea consumption, as documented by a comprehensive survey of EGCG content across 36 commercial varieties. These findings support PAR-2 as a candidate upstream target of EGCG in OA chondrocytes and suggest a mechanistic model involving PAR-2 → ERK1/2 → TNF-α/SOX4/ADAMTS-5, through which a dietary polyphenol exerts coordinated anti-inflammatory and anti-catabolic effects, while preserving structural and thermodynamic markers of mitochondrial integrity.

metadata.title: Intensity-dependent microcurrent stimulation enhances BMSC-derived cartilage microtissue formation under defined culture conditions.
metadata.abstract: Engineering phenotypically favorable cartilage-like tissue from bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) remains challenging because chondrogenic differentiation can be accompanied by insufficient cartilage-associated extracellular matrix accumulation and unfavorable hypertrophic and catabolic responses. Here, we established a microcurrent-assisted culture system for scaffold-free BMSC-derived cartilage microtissues (CMTs) and investigated the intensity-dependent effects of continuous unidirectional direct-current stimulation at 0, 50, 100, 150, 250, or 500 μA under a defined electrical and culture configuration. Among the tested conditions, 150 μA (nominal electrode current density, 3 μA/mm2) showed the most consistently favorable overall response, with enhanced cartilage-associated gene and protein expression, greater type II collagen- and glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix accumulation, improved CMT morphology, and higher apparent mechanical properties. In contrast, 250 and 500 μA were associated with reduced cartilage-associated matrix formation and increased fibrotic, hypertrophic, catabolic, inflammatory, and apoptosis-related markers. The 150 μA condition was also associated with a distinct intracellular Ca2+ response pattern and increased NFATc1 nuclear localization; verapamil, BAPTA-AM, and cyclosporin A attenuated NFATc1 nuclear localization, supporting involvement of Ca2+/calcineurin/NFAT-related signaling without establishing a unique causal mechanism. After 2 weeks of xenogeneic subcutaneous implantation in nude mice, CMTs preconditioned at 150 μA exhibited greater cartilage-like matrix accumulation and higher apparent compressive properties than those preconditioned at 0 or 500 μA. These findings identify 150 μA as the best-performing tested condition under the present electrical configuration and provide short-term ectopic proof-of-concept evidence, while longer-term orthotopic studies are required to evaluate phenotypic stability, tissue integration, and functional outcomes in cartilage-defect models.

metadata.title: A Six-Day High-Intensity Interval Training Microcycle Improves Selected Indicators of Endurance Performance in Well-Trained Female Cross-Country Skiers and Biathletes.
metadata.abstract: We compared the effects of a 6-day high-intensity interval training (HIT) microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period (HITblock) with a time-matched period of continued regular training (REG) on endurance performance in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes. Seventeen athletes (maximal oxygen consumption ( V ˙ O 2 max ): 55.1 (5.2) mL·min-1 kg-1) were assigned to either HITblock or REG. No differences in training volume or intensity were observed between the groups during the 4 weeks preceding the intervention. During the intervention, HITblock completed five HIT sessions over 6 days (6 × 5-min work intervals; target rate of perceived exertion:17-18), with increased HIT replacing part of their habitual training and thereby reducing overall training load, whereas REG continued habitual training, including 3-4 moderate- or high-intensity interval sessions. Endurance performance was assessed during roller ski skating and included 15-min time-trial average velocity (velocity15-min), velocity at 4 mmol·L-1 blood lactate (velocity4mmol), and velocity during the final minute of incremental V ˙ O 2 max testing ( velocity V ˙ O 2 max ). HITblock demonstrated greater improvements than REG in velocity V ˙ O 2 max (3.6 (2.1)% versus 1.2 (1.6)%, p = 0.024) and velocity4mmol (4.4 (2.9)% versus 0.0 (4.4)%, p = 0.023), whereas changes in velocity15-min did not differ between groups (5.4 (5.0)% versus 1.3 (3.4)%, p = 0.083). An exploratory composite performance index combining these outcomes demonstrated superior improvements in HITblock compared with REG (4.5 (2.8)% versus 0.9 (2.6)%, p = 0.017). These findings indicate that a 6-day HIT microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period is associated with greater improvements in selected endurance performance indicators compared with continued regular training in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes.

metadata.title: A rare traumatic triad: Open bicondylar non-conjoint Hoffa fracture with partial tibial tubercle and medial epicondyle avulsions - A case report and biomechanical analysis.
metadata.abstract: UNLABELLED: Coronal shear fractures of the distal femoral condyles are rare intra-articular injuries, and the simultaneous occurrence of a non-conjoint bicondylar Hoffa fracture with a partial anterior tibial tubercle avulsion and a medial epicondyle avulsion constitutes an exceptionally complex traumatic triad. We report the case of a 35-year-old male motorcyclist who sustained this "floating" articular block injury (AO/OTA 33-B3.3) following a high-velocity accident. Diagnostic assessment utilizing Computed Tomography with 3D reconstruction revealed a vertical Letenneur Type II fracture of the medial condyle and a comminuted Letenneur Type I fracture of the lateral condyle, complicated by significant rotational instability. Surgical management prioritized the posterior femoral instability through a double posterior approach, which allowed for direct visualization and anatomical reduction. Fixation was achieved using posterior-to-anterior headless compression screws, augmented by a posterior buttress plate on the lateral column to neutralize shear forces, while the medial epicondyle was anatomically reduced and fixed; the stable partial tibial tubercle avulsion was treated conservatively. At the two-year follow-up, the patient demonstrated excellent functional recovery with 120 degrees of flexion, a Lysholm score of 91, and a successful return to recreational sports. This case highlights the importance of the double posterior approach and "targeted rigidity" in managing multidirectional instability, permitting early mobilization even in the presence of complex extensor mechanism involvement. INTRODUCTION: Coronal shear fractures of the distal femoral condyles (Hoffa fractures) are rare intra-articular injuries, with bicondylar patterns being exceptionally uncommon. A non-conjoint bicondylar Hoffa fracture combined with a partial anterior tibial tubercle (ATT) avulsion and a medial epicondyle avulsion represents a complex, "floating" articular block that challenges standard treatment algorithms. This case report analyzes the biomechanics and management of this rare traumatic triad. CASE PRESENTATION: A 35-year-old male motorcyclist presented with a Gustilo-Anderson Type I open knee injury following a high-velocity crash involving hyper-flexion and valgus stress. CT imaging confirmed a non-conjoint bicondylar Hoffa fracture (AO/OTA 33-B3.3, Bagaria Type 3). The lateral condyle presented as a Letenneur Type I fracture with extensive comminution, while the medial condyle was a Letenneur Type II vertical fracture. Associated injuries included an Ogden Type I partial ATT avulsion and a Watson-Jones Type I medial epicondyle avulsion.Surgical management utilized a double posterior approach to visualize and reduce the posterior fragments. Fixation involved headless cannulated compression screws for both condyles, augmented by a posterior buttress plate on the lateral column to resist shear forces. The medial epicondyle was refixed with a screw and washer, while the stable ATT avulsion was managed conservatively. At the two-year follow-up, the patient achieved excellent functional outcomes, including 120° of flexion, a Lysholm score of 91, and a Tegner Activity Scale score of 7. CONCLUSION: Managing this complex triad requires a thorough understanding of the injury mechanism, which involves coronal shear, valgus stress, and eccentric extensor loading. 3D CT reconstruction is mandatory for planning, and a double posterior approach provides superior visualization for anatomical reduction and posterior-to-anterior fixation. Rigid fixation, particularly using anti-glide plating for the lateral column, permits early mobilization and the conservative management of stable associated injuries, leading to high patient satisfaction.

metadata.title: Are both hemolysis and impaired myocyte integrity associated with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency?
metadata.abstract: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) is a potent antioxidant enzyme. G6PD deficiency, predominant among males, is a neonatal "neurotoxic" risk, characterized by episodic hemolysis that is sometimes infection triggered. Clinical risk among heterozygous G6PD-deficient females is often under-recognized. Recent reports of rhabdomyolysis among G6PD-deficient individuals are reviewed here. In one case, a male athlete with G6PD deficiency (<10% activity) experienced multiple, acute episodes of rhabdomyolysis, painful muscle symptomatology, injury and hemolysis after strenuous exertion. Both his mother with G6PD-deficiency (<45% activity) and maternal grandmother have chronic histories of episodic or triggered fatigue-related disruptive symptoms. Other case reports of G6PD-deficient individuals with muscle injury and exertional symptoms (with or without hemolysis) showed unique laboratory findings of elevated creatine kinase, myoglobin, lactate dehydrogenase, creatinine, and aminotransferases levels and myoglobinuria. Disrupted myocyte energetics and loss of cellular integrity can be attributed to impaired downstream pentose phosphate pathway (PPP)-related oxidant stress protection, which is a key enzymatic consequence of G6PD-deficiency. These triggered stresses may explain the muscle fatigue and propensity to exertional injury. Correlation between stress-sensitive-impaired muscle injury among all G6PD-deficient individuals, including neonates, requires further clinical validation to ascertain oxidant-stress impact of impaired PPP-dependent cellular energetics of red blood, white blood, neural, and muscle cells.

metadata.title: Beware the Muscle: Silent Exercise-Induced Aminotransferase Elevation as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Hepatology and Pretreatment Screening-A Report of Two Cases.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: In clinical hepatology practice, pretreatment liver enzyme screening plays a key role in making management decisions, such as initiation of antituberculosis therapy or surveillance of chronic hepatitis B. Unrecognized extrahepatic sources of aminotransferase elevations can lead to misdiagnosis, inappropriate treatment alteration, and unnecessary invasive or costly investigations. CASE PRESENTATION: We present two cases of active young males who were undergoing liver biochemical testing for therapeutic decision-making for other underlying illnesses. Patient one was undergoing baseline liver enzyme testing prior to first-line antituberculosis treatment initiation while patient two was undergoing surveillance for e-antigen-negative hepatitis B infection. Both patients had asymptomatic aminotransferase elevations mimicking acute hepatocellular injury. There was a marked and disproportionate elevation of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) relative to alanine aminotransferase (ALT), in the setting of otherwise normal cholestatic and synthetic parameters. Targeted history revealed heavy resistance weight training prior to testing. Measurement of serum creatine kinase (CK) confirmed exercise-induced muscle injury, demonstrating elevated CK concentrations that paralleled the AST trajectory. Cessation of strenuous training led to rapid normalization of aminotransferases and a decline in CK levels, without interruption of tuberculosis management or unwarranted antiviral initiation. CONCLUSION: Clinically silent exertional muscle injury is an underappreciated mimicker of acute liver injury. In patients presenting with isolated or disproportionate AST elevation, confirming a myogenic enzyme source via CK quantification can prevent misdiagnosis, eliminate unnecessary liver-directed workup, and avoid inappropriate modification or initiation of essential pharmacotherapy.

metadata.title: Neuromuscular Fatigue and Recovery: Are Marathon and Trail Running Different?
metadata.abstract: Although trail and road are two running disciplines, they have distinct characteristics potentially leading to different physiological impacts that have never been examined. The aim of the present study was to compare neuromuscular fatigue and recovery between a marathon and two trail runs of equivalent effort (29 km; ± 1,400 m). Forty-one trained runners, specialized in either road or trail running, performed a simulated treadmill marathon (MARASIM), a simulated treadmill trail run (TRAILSIM), or a trail run in natural conditions (TRAILNAT), depending on their speciality. Neuromuscular fatigue, i.e. changes in maximal voluntary contraction (MVC), voluntary activation (VA) and peak twitch (Tw) of the knee extensors (KE) and plantar flexors (PF), blood markers of muscle damage, jump performance, and force-velocity profile (FVP) were assessed before (PRE), immediately after (POST), one (+1 day), two (+2 days), and seven days (+7 days) following the runs. Muscle pain questionnaires were administered at PRE and during the month following the run. MARASIM showed significantly greater decreases in KE VA (-23.5% vs. -9.2% vs. -13.0%) and jump height (-11.7%; +11.4%; +5.9%, for squat jump), and significantly higher increases in blood markers of muscle damage (+1,726 UI.L -1; +641 UI.L -1; +363 UI.L -1; at +1 day) compared to TRAILSIM and TRAILNAT, respectively. The return to baseline occurred later in MARASIM for KE VA and jump height. Muscle soreness values also returned to baseline earlier in TRAILNAT and TRAILSIM compared to MARASIM. No differences between groups existed in KE Pt and MVC, in any PF neuromuscular fatigue variables, and FVP. Overall, marathon running appears to induce greater acute neuromuscular alterations than trail running, mostly on KE, with a slower return to baseline values.

metadata.title: Balneotherapy in knee osteoarthritis: a review of therapeutic efficacy and inflammatory cytokine regulation.
metadata.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common degenerative joint disease with an inflammatory component. Balneotherapy has been used for KOA, but its clinical efficacy and mechanisms remain uncertain. This narrative review summarizes clinical evidence and proposes a hypothesis-generating mechanistic framework. PubMed and CNKI were searched up to June 2026. Interventions were categorized as mineral-water bathing, aquatic exercise/hydrotherapy, mud therapy/pelotherapy, or multimodal spa programmes, and clinical studies were assessed for risk of bias. Randomized trials and meta-analyses suggest that balneotherapy may improve short-term pain and function, with benefits reportedly persisting for 3-9 months in some studies; however, most trials had high risk of bias, heterogeneous protocols, small samples, and short follow-up. Mechanistic evidence is largely preclinical or indirect. H₂S has the most consistent anti-inflammatory and anti-catabolic rationale, acting via NF-κB and MMP-13 inhibition. Calcium and magnesium may modulate TRPV4/NLRP3 and NF-κB signaling, but human balneotherapy evidence is lacking, and mineral synergy remains unverified. A three-tier "heat-mineral-signal" framework is proposed, but target engagement after bathing and causality between biomarker changes and clinical improvement have not been established. Overall, balneotherapy may offer symptomatic benefits in KOA, but current evidence is limited and heterogeneous. The proposed mechanistic model is hypothesis-generating; higher-quality trials with standardized protocols, long-term follow-up, and integrated clinical and mechanistic outcomes are needed.

metadata.title: Gender Differences in Sports Injuries of the Foot and Ankle.
metadata.abstract: This article examines sex-based differences in foot and ankle injuries among female athletes, emphasizing the role of anatomic, hormonal, biomechanical, and sociocultural factors. Conditions such as relative energy deficiency in sport and the female athlete triad contribute to injury risk and long-term health consequences but remain under-recognized. This article highlights disparities in research, treatment, and outcomes, calling for improved screening, sex-specific prevention strategies, and greater inclusion of female subjects in sports medicine research to inform evidence-based care and optimize outcomes for female athletes.

metadata.title: Metabolic Bone Health in Female Patients: Focus on Foot and Ankle.
metadata.abstract: Metabolic bone health is crucial for the overall well-being of female patients. Female athletes and young females are of particular interest, as their skeletal systems are still developing and are sensitive to the hormonal and physical stress of training and diet. Stress fractures occur with higher frequency in females with risk factors such as low bone mineral density (BMD). When low bone mineral density occurs along with menstrual irregularities and relative energy deficiency, it completes the female triad (23, 27, and 28). Any discussion of female BMD and metabolic bone health must include the female triad.

metadata.title: The Sleep and Diet of Elite Female Australian Rules Football Athletes Differ With Age and Season Phase.
metadata.abstract: The Australian Football League Women's (AFLW) competition is comprised of a short, intensive competitive season, highlighting the importance of proper fuelling and recovery to support performance. Little is known about the dietary and sleep habits of AFLW athletes across a season, and the influence that age has on these behaviours. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the effects of season phase and age on dietary intake and sleep in elite AFLW athletes. Dietary intake and sleep were assessed in 22 AFLW athletes (25.9 ± 5.0 y) over 10 nights, including five consecutive nights during both pre-season and in-season. Dietary intake was quantified through self-reported food diaries using a smartphone application (Easy Diet Diary), and sleep via a wearable monitoring device (Oura ring). Restricted maximum likelihood mixed models were used to determine variations in dietary intake and sleep in AFLW players between season phases (i.e., pre-season vs. in-season) and age. In-season protein (115.15 ± 35.14 vs. 126.48 ± 40.10 g, p = 0.026) and fat intakes (72.93 ± 29.55 vs. 83.43 ± 33.14 g, p = 0.012) were significantly lower compared to pre-season, with no differences in sleep measures observed between season phases. While age did not influence dietary intake, each additional year of age was associated with 8 min less sleep (p = 0.001) and 4 min earlier wake times (p = 0.032). These findings suggest that protein and fat intakes fluctuate across the seasons, with increasing age being a non-modifiable risk factor for shorter sleep durations within AFLW athletes.

metadata.title: Use of 2.5% polyacrylamide hydrogel mitigates joint capsule stiffness and cartilage degradation in experimental equine osteoarthritis.
metadata.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the symptom- and disease-modifying effects of injectable 2.5% polyacrylamide gel (iPAAG) in an experimental model of equine osteoarthritis (OA). METHODS: 16 horses underwent osteochondral fragment creation (day 0) in 1 randomly-selected middle carpal joint (MCJ). On day 14, the MCJ was injected with 2 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (n = 8) or 2.5% iPAAG (8); high-speed treadmill exercise commenced on day 16 to induce OA. Clinical parameters (lameness, joint effusion, range of motion, flexion response) and synovial fluid were collected weekly and biweekly, respectively. Radiographs were obtained before surgery, at day 14, and at day 70. Postmortem evaluation (day 70) included gross, arthroscopic, and histopathologic evaluation of the MCJs and measurement of joint capsule stiffness. RESULTS: There were no significant differences in clinical parameters or endpoint arthroscopic, macroscopic, or synovial membrane histopathology scores between groups. In 2.5% iPAAG-treated limbs, the third carpal bone had significantly lower (better) total articular cartilage histology scores (6.38 ± 4.10 vs 11.25 ± 4.20) and proteoglycan staining scores of the intermediate articular cartilage layer (0.38 ± 0.74 vs 1.88 ± 1.25) compared to saline-treated OA joints. Saline-treated OA joints had significantly increased joint capsule stiffness versus contralateral sham-operated MCJs (1,824 ± 1,105 vs 1,002 ± 495 Pa), whereas 2.5% iPAAG-treated joints did not (1,099 ± 647 vs 1,184 ± 504 Pa). CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with 2.5% iPAAG showed some ability to mitigate the negative effects of OA on articular cartilage. Treatment also resulted in retention of normal joint capsule elasticity during the progression of OA. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Treatment with 2.5% iPAAG may result in retention of normal joint capsule elasticity in horses with naturally occurring OA.

metadata.title: Articular Cartilage-Derived Extracellular Matrix Material Promotes a Pro-Regenerative Macrophage Phenotype to Support Chondrogenesis.
metadata.abstract: Articular cartilage (AC) repair remains a major clinical challenge due to its limited healing capacity and the inability of current treatment strategies to restore long-term function. Biomaterial-based strategies which support favorable immune responses and appropriate progenitor cell function have shown promise in enhancing cartilage regeneration. We and others have previously demonstrated the capacity of extracellular matrix (ECM)-based materials to direct both innate immune cell behavior and progenitor cell differentiation, with these effects highly dependent on the ECM tissue of origin. Building on these observations, we now aim to further investigate the immunomodulatory properties of AC-derived ECM (AC-ECM) materials. Using primary human macrophages, we demonstrate that AC-ECM material promotes a metabolically active mixed response in macrophages, with elevated expression of reparative growth factors conducive to chondrogenesis. Furthermore, AC-ECM limits inflammatory activation of primary human macrophages, as demonstrated by reduced metabolic reprogramming and inflammatory cytokine production. Functionally, macrophages treated with AC-ECM enhance cartilage regeneration by increasing chondrogenic marker expression in mesenchymal stem cells, while also suppressing angiogenic tube formation in endothelial cells. Overall, this work demonstrates that AC-ECM biomaterials can direct macrophage phenotype toward a pro-chondrogenic state, offering a promising strategy for the development of more effective and durable cartilage repair therapies.

metadata.title: Extracellular vesicles: Multi-source regulatory mechanisms in hippocampal homeostasis.
metadata.abstract: Hippocampal health is pivotal for memory, emotional regulation, and cognition. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) facilitate intercellular and inter-organ communication by transporting bioactive cargos; however, traditional research often overlooks systemic influences on the hippocampus in favor of local microenvironmental changes. This review synthesizes evidence demonstrating that hippocampal homeostasis is modulated by the organism's systemic state-including aging, obesity, and immune status-via EVs. We detail mechanisms by which EVs from peripheral organs (adipose tissue, gut/microbiota, lung, bone, muscle, liver, kidney, heart, and spleen) and central nervous system resident cells (neurons, microglia, astrocytes, neural stem cells, and endothelial cells) regulate hippocampal function. These multi-source EVs precisely modulate neurogenesis, inflammatory responses, and synaptic plasticity. Furthermore, we highlight the emerging role of migrasomes as a specialized subset of EVs in this regulatory landscape. By mapping this comprehensive EV-mediated network, we provide a holistic perspective on the crosstalk between the systemic environment and the hippocampus, offering novel insights and therapeutic strategies for diseases associated with hippocampal dysfunction.

metadata.title: 660 nm LED preconditioning programs mitochondrial signaling in BMSCs for functional tracheal cartilage regeneration.
metadata.abstract: Stem-cell-based cartilage regeneration is limited not only by cell delivery, but also by the difficulty of establishing a stable and functionally competent regenerative cell state before implantation. Here, we report a photonic mitochondrial programming strategy in which 660 nm light-emitting diode (LED) irradiation preconditions bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) to enhance functional tracheal cartilage regeneration. BMSCs were seeded onto egg white-derived ring-shaped porous scaffolds and exposed to defined 660 nm LED irradiation before implantation. Among the tested irradiation conditions, 15 J/cm2 optimally promoted BMSC proliferation, chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage-like extracellular matrix deposition, while suppressing fibrotic, hypertrophic and matrix-degrading phenotypes. Mechanistically, 660 nm LED irradiation enhanced cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) activity, mitochondrial membrane potential, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production and respiratory function, accompanied by moderate reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling. This mitochondrial bioenergetic-redox response activated the PI3K/Akt/mTOR/GSK3β-SOX9 axis, thereby promoting type II collagen, aggrecan and glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix formation. Pharmacological inhibition of ROS signaling, mitochondrial activity, PI3K or mTOR attenuated the LED-induced chondrogenic program. In a rabbit tracheal cartilage ring defect model, 15 J/cm2-preconditioned BMSC-scaffold constructs improved cartilage-like tissue formation, airway epithelial repair, lumen patency and mechanical support after 30 days of observation. These findings support 660 nm LED irradiation as a controllable mitochondrial preconditioning strategy for stem-cell-based functional cartilage regeneration.

metadata.title: Clonal articular cartilage progenitors outperform mesenchymal stromal cells in mitigating post-traumatic osteoarthritis.
metadata.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the functional, pathological, and immunomodulatory properties of articular chondroprogenitors (ACPs) with those of bone-marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) in preventing the progression of post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) after destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) injury in a mouse model. METHOD: ACP and MSC were isolated from three horses and assessed for their immunomodulatory capacity in vitro. Aliquots of selected ACP clones and MSCs were injected intra-articularly into male mice 1-week post destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM). The functional mobility of the mice before the injury and at weeks 2, 4, and 8 post-injury was assessed by two methods: ANY-maze™ voluntary mobility monitoring and DigiGait™ compulsory gait analysis. Upon euthanasia, joints were collected for histological scoring. RESULTS: In vitro assessments demonstrated that ACPs and MSCs had anti-inflammatory properties: both treatments produced lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, while only the ACPs produced more anti-inflammatory cytokines than controls. In vivo, both ACPs and MSCs lessened the effects of DMM on mobility. Histological scoring revealed significant reductions of PTOA in the medial compartment with ACPs relative to both MSCs and vehicle controls. Overall, ACPs effectively reduced PTOA progression to a greater extent than MSCs. CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrated that both equine ACP and MSC treatments provided symptom modification over vehicle controls in a short-term animal study. Notably, ACPs may be more efficacious than MSCs at reducing structural joint pathology.

metadata.title: EMSCs-derived exosomes rescue p75NTR-/- -mediated osteogenesis deficiency via PI3K/Akt/ERK1/2 signaling pathways.
metadata.abstract: The repair of the critical-sized bone defects remains a major challenge for orthopedic surgeons, particularly when osteogenesis is impaired by p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR) deficiency. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are not fully understood. This study aimed to clarify the role of p75NTR in bone regeneration and to develop a cell-free approach to rescue p75NTR-/- deficiency-mediated osteogenic deficiency through a controlled releasing of wild-type ectomesenchymal stem cells exosomes (WT-Exo) which were incorporated into silk fibroin/polycaprolactone2:5/polyvinyl alcohol (SF/PCL2:5/PVA) coaxial nanofibrous membranes. p75NTR-/- mice exhibited a reduced bone mass and delayed ossification, while WT-Exo-loaded membranes partially restored osteogenic deficiency in p75NTR-/- cells and enhanced expression of osteogenic markers such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP), collagen type I (Col-I), osteopontin (OPN) and runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2) aaccompanied by activating of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) signaling pathway. Following implantation of the WT-Exo-loaded membranes into the critical-sized cranial defects in p75NTR-/- mice, new bone formation in the defect site was significantly improved by a sustained release of WT-Exo. Overall, the findings in this study highlighted the critical role of p75NTR in osteogenic differentiation of ectomesenchymal stem cells (EMSCs) and demonstrated that WT-Exo, delivered via the coaxial electrospun membranes, represented an effective cell-free intervention method to reverse bone formation deficiency caused by p75NTR deficiency, providing a promising strategy for gene deficiency-related bone diseases.

metadata.title: Advancing regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies in orthopaedic traumatology.
metadata.abstract: The 2025 Orthopaedic Trauma Association's Basic Science Focus Forum featured a symposium on regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies for orthopaedic trauma. Four experts presented complementary perspectives on the next generation of bone and soft tissue repair: Dr. J. Tracy Watson described how orthobiologics and refined spacer design can be used to engineer a better Masquelet induced membrane; Dr. Lauren Priddy presented evidence that hydroxyapatite coatings can mitigate the rapid degradation of additively manufactured magnesium scaffolds; Dr. Vaida Glatt described the development and clinical translation of the Biomimetic Hematoma scaffold for bone and muscle regeneration; and Dr. Katherine Hixon outlined how the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) can serve as a framework to accelerate musculoskeletal regenerative engineering. Collectively, the symposium underscored a shift toward biologically informed, clinically predictive, and ethically responsible engineering solutions for the patients who sustain musculoskeletal trauma.

metadata.title: PTHrP suppresses BMP2-induced osteochondral differentiation and preserves cartilage phenotype in mesenchymal stem cells via inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling.
metadata.abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2) has the potential to drive multipotent mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) to undergo chondral-osteogenic (including hypertrophic chondrocyte) differentiation. Parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) plays an essential role in fetal endochondral ossification, although persistent PTHrP stimulation leads to postnatal bone loss. Here, we investigated the effects of PTHrP on BMP2-induced endochondral ossification through hypertrophic chondrocyte differentiation of MSCs. We found that silencing PTHrP expression inhibited BMP2-induced chondrogenic, hypertrophic, and osteogenic differentiation of MSCs, while overexpression of PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs and suppressed BMP2-induced hypertrophic differentiation of MSCs. Using stem cell implantation studies in athymic nude mice, we demonstrated that while MSCs with silenced PTHrP expression exhibited significantly reduced endochondral ossification of subcutaneous cartilage, overexpression of PTHrP promoted the growth of subcutaneous cartilage while significantly delaying ossification, leading to the preservation of cartilage phenotype. Mechanistically, we showed that exogenous PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs by up-regulating Sox9 expression and inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling. Collectively, our findings strongly suggest that PTHrP may play an important role in mediating BMP2-induced chondral-osteogenic differentiation of MSCs by inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling, indicating that PTHrP may be exploited for endochondral cartilage-bone tissue engineering.

metadata.title: Targeting the lactate/P300/H3K18la epigenetic pathway with a mechanoadaptive biomimetic hydrogel to suppress traumatic tendon heterotopic ossification.
metadata.abstract: Traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a debilitating complication of tendon injury, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain elusive and effective preventive strategies are lacking. Here, we identify a glycometabolic-epigenetic axis that drives HO progression. Single-cell profiling and functional analyses reveal that hypoxic chondrocytes undergo glycolytic reprogramming, leading to lactate accumulation and transfer into tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TD-MSCs) through MCT1. This metabolic coupling promotes P300-dependent histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), activating osteogenic programs characterized by Col6a1, Zhx3, Lox and Vdr expression and thereby facilitating pathological endochondral ossification. Guided by this mechanism, we develop a tendon-adhesive hydrogel (GelHA-A485@Exos) that integrates mechanical repair with targeted epigenetic modulation. MSC-derived exosomes enable localized delivery of the P300 inhibitor A485, suppressing H3K18la and aberrant osteogenic activation, while the hydrogel scaffold enhances tendon regeneration. In vivo and in vitro studies demonstrate that GelHA-A485@Exos promotes tendon healing while preventing HO formation. Our findings establish metabolic-epigenetic communication as a central regulator of traumatic HO and provide a translational therapeutic strategy for its clinical prevention.

metadata.title: Supporting adolescent menstrual health to improve participation and performance in physical activity: rapid realist review to inform a logic model for intervention development.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Insufficient physical activity is higher in women and girls globally, with increased risk of non-communicable diseases. Menstrual (period-related) symptoms are a recognised barrier to adolescents engaging in physical activity. There is a lack of evidence-based guidance to address this barrier. OBJECTIVE: To develop a set of initial programme theories (context-mechanism-outcome configurations, CMOCs) to describe how existing menstrual health support interventions work, for whom, how and in what circumstances to inform a logic model for intervention development. DESIGN: Rapid realist review. METHODS: Formal, double-screened, database (Medline, AMED, Embase, Psycinfo, CINAHL, ERIC, SCOPUS; June 2025) and grey literature searches guided by stakeholder expertise. Articles were selected that met inclusion criteria and contributed to theory development. Explanatory statements were extracted and synthesised into CMOCs using Pawson’s reasoning processes and mapped onto Self-Determination Theory concepts (autonomy, competency, relatedness). RESULTS: From 9585 database hits, 63 articles were included. Three generated initial programme theories describe how four identified intervention domains (education; practicalities including toilet facilities, clothing and free accessible period products; menstrual cycle tracking and screening tools; and medical support if needed) could improve menstrual health confidence and understanding (M), communication and trust (M)—to empower individuals to enhance their own menstrual health (M) and potentially improve participation rates and performance in physical activity (O). Alternative causal pathways describe potential adverse outcomes when processes are not in place to: signpost to medical support if needed (M), support user trust in how and why data are collected and used (M) and enable understanding of the limitations of menstrual health support tools (M). Contextual data are needed to further refine these theories that are presented as a logic model. CONCLUSION: The proposed logic model can be used to inform and evaluate future interventions aimed at overcoming menstrual health related barriers with physical activity. PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420251066742.

metadata.title: Restoring the repair-fibrosis balance via a localized extracellular vesicle-pirfenidone dual-delivery biomaterial platform promotes ureteral repair after thermal injury.
metadata.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Ureteral thermal injury can lead to ureteral stricture through persistent oxidative stress, inflammation, impaired vascular repair, and excessive fibrosis. Current treatment strategies primarily aim to restore urinary drainage or address established structural obstruction, whereas approaches that simultaneously modulate tissue repair and postinjury fibrotic remodeling remain limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop a localized dual-delivery biomaterial platform that simultaneously promotes tissue repair and suppresses excessive fibrosis after ureteral thermal injury. METHODS: A localized EG_PFM platform was fabricated by combining a mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicle (MSC-EV)-loaded chitosan/hyaluronic acid hydrogel (EG) with a pirfenidone (PF)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) nanofibrous membrane (PFM). The physicochemical properties and release profiles were characterized. In vitro, the effects of MSC-EVs and PF on urothelial and smooth muscle cell relative cell growth and migration, oxidative stress, angiogenesis, macrophage phenotype, and fibrosis-associated cellular responses were evaluated. A rabbit model of ureteral thermal injury was established to assess ureteral structural repair, hydronephrosis, collagen deposition, oxidative stress, inflammation, angiogenesis, and transcriptomic changes. RESULTS: EG_PFM exhibited favorable biocompatibility, tissue adhesion, and sustained release of MSC-EVs and PF. MSC-EVs increased relative cell growth and enhanced the migration of urothelial and smooth muscle cells, reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species, enhanced endothelial tube formation and were associated with an M2-like macrophage phenotype, whereas PF suppressed α-SMA expression and extracellular matrix accumulation. In rabbits, EG_PFM reduced hydronephrosis and ureteral stricture, decreased collagen deposition, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses, and enhanced vascularization. Transcriptomic analysis identified treatment-associated changes in multiple signaling and metabolic pathways, including calcium signaling, cell adhesion molecules, tyrosine metabolism, and retinol metabolism. CONCLUSION: Localized codelivery of MSC-EVs and PF promoted reparative responses while limiting fibrotic remodeling, thereby improving structural repair after ureteral thermal injury. EG_PFM represents a promising localized therapeutic strategy for reducing postinjury ureteral stricture.

metadata.title: Evaluation of a four-herb Chinese medicine formula at different concentrations on muscle damage and inflammation in a rat model of DOMS.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) impairs exercise recovery, while current treatments remain limited. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulas may provide safe, multi-target interventions. OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the dose-dependent protective effects of a four-herb Chinese medicine formulation (safflower, Chinese Angelica, peach kernel and myrrh) against DOMS in a rat model. METHODS: Thirty-two male SPF SD rats were randomly allocated to control or low- (1696 mg/kg), medium- (3392 mg/kg), or high-dose (6784 mg/kg) groups. The formulation was administered orally for 11 days, with DOMS induced by exhaustive swimming on day 8. Serum CK, Mb, CRP, IL-6, and PGE2 were measured at baseline and at 24, 48, 72, and 96 h post-exercise. RESULTS: The medium- and high-dose groups exhibited significantly lower serum CK, Mb, CRP, IL-6, and PGE2 levels than controls, with the high-dose group showing the largest reductions. The low-dose group showed limited or no significant reductions in most markers, demonstrating a clear dose-dependent protective effect. CONCLUSIONS: The formulation dose-dependently attenuates muscle damage and inflammation in a rat DOMS model, with high-dose treatment achieving the fastest recovery. Clinical trials are warranted to confirm the efficacy and safety in humans.

metadata.title: M4-like Macrophages Drive Skeletal Muscle Fibrosis and Suppress Myogenesis via the MMP12/SPP1/NF-κB Axis.
metadata.abstract: Acute skeletal muscle repair depends on a finely tuned balance between myogenic regeneration and fibrotic remodeling. Macrophages are essential to this process, and specific subsets have been linked to fibrosis in some organs. The M4-like macrophage, a distinct polarization subset implicated in fibrotic diseases, has not been well characterized in the context of injured muscle, particularly regarding its impact on fibroblast activation and myogenic suppression. The study aims to explore the effects of M4-like macrophages in the repair of muscle injury and possible mechanism. We analyzed a murine single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset from cardiotoxin (CTX)-injured skeletal muscle to identify injury-expanded macrophage subsets and their molecular programs. Immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence staining of muscle sections were used to assess CXCL4 expression and platelet (CD41+) infiltration in injured versus uninjured tissues. CXCL4-induced M4-like macrophages were established as an in vitro model to examine their effects on L929 fibroblasts and C2C12 myoblasts. The MMP12-SPP1 interaction was predicted by AlphaFold3 and validated by co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence colocalization. Loss-of-function and rescue experiments targeting MMP12 and SPP1 were performed to determine their causal roles in fibroblast activation and myogenic suppression. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses were used to define downstream macrophage-intrinsic NF-κB/TNF-α signaling. Finally, AAV-mediated macrophage-targeted SPP1 knockdown and pharmacological NF-κB inhibition were evaluated in the CTX injury model. Using a BALB/c mouse model of cardiotoxin (CTX)-induced acute skeletal muscle injury and a publicly available murine scRNA-seq dataset from CTX-injured skeletal muscle, we observed an injury-induced MMP12/SPP1-positive macrophage subset with an M4-like transcriptional signature. Mechanistically, co-immunoprecipitation assays and immunofluorescence colocalization supported an association between MMP12 and SPP1. MMP12 knockdown attenuated the pro-fibrotic and anti-myogenic effects of M4-like macrophages, whereas recombinant SPP1 largely restored these phenotypes. Furthermore, transcriptomic and biochemical analyses revealed that autocrine SPP1 activated NF-κB signaling in M4-like macrophages, and increased TNF-α secretion. Pharmacological inhibition of NF-κB signaling with QNZ reduced fibroblast activation and restored the expression of myogenic markers. However, QNZ is not TNF-α specific and may affect multiple cell types. In vivo, AAV-mediated macrophage-targeted SPP1 knockdown driven by the F4/80 promoter, as well as QNZ treatment in the CTX-induced muscle injury model, markedly decreased collagen deposition, enhanced myogenic regeneration, and improved functional recovery. These findings identify an MMP12/SPP1/NF-κB signaling pathway in M4-like macrophages, with TNF-α as a potential downstream mediator, that may contribute to an imbalance between regeneration and fibrosis and may represent a therapeutic target for enhancing skeletal muscle repair after acute injury.

metadata.title: Binding of a Novel 11β-Hydroxysteroid to the Apelin Receptor (APLNR) and Its Possible Role in Regulating Skeletal Muscle Health in Mice.
metadata.abstract: Several molecules have been investigated for their potential to improve muscle health in models of muscle damage simulating sarcopenia, injury, or aging. Some small molecules induced beneficial effects on skeletal muscle by stimulating the apelin receptor (APLNR). This receptor has emerged as a promising pharmacological target for modulating muscle homeostasis. Using an in silico approach, we recently identified 11β-hydroxypregnenolone (11β-OHP5) as a potential skeletal muscle (SKM) modulator. We hypothesized that 11β-OHP5 interacts with and activates APLNR. This study employed several research approaches: (1) in silico molecular docking and molecular dynamics to explore the feasibility of 11β-OHP5 interacting with APLNR; (2) in vitro activation analysis to APLNR; (3) in vitro analysis C2C12 myoblast differentiation; (4) analysis of the molecule's presence in mouse skeletal muscle and its differential presence between young and older mice. The results show that 11β-OHP5, acting through APLNR, positively affects myoblast differentiation and may participate in the exercise-induced benefits in aging mice. We show that 11β-OHP5 interacts with APLNR, induces myogenic responses, is found in SKM; its concentration decreases with age, and exercise restores it. More work is necessary to understand the physiology of this possible endogenous molecule.

metadata.title: Effects of Intramuscular Mesenchymal Stem Cell and Boric Acid Administration on Muscle Damage and Recovery in an Exhaustive Swimming Rat Model.
metadata.abstract: Exhaustive exercise induces damage to skeletal muscle, reducing athletic performance and delaying recovery. Effective experimental strategies are needed to mitigate this damage and accelerate tissue regeneration. This study aimed to address limitations in the therapeutic efficacy of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal/stem cell-like cells (MSCs) associated with limited cell viability by evaluating boric acid (BA) as an antioxidant and metabolic modulator to enhance cell viability and muscle repair. Twenty-five female Wistar albino rats underwent a 15 day exhaustive swimming protocol and received intramuscular injections of MSCs (1 × 106 cells), BA (10 µg), or their combination, according to the experimental group allocation. Bone marrow obtained from five additional donor rats was used exclusively for MSC isolation and culture. Daily exhaustion time, serum biomarkers lactate, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), creatine kinase (CK), and gastrocnemius histology were evaluated. Intramuscular BA improved endurance and reduced biochemical markers of muscle injury, whereas MSC application promoted structural muscle regeneration, as evidenced by centrally located nuclei and improved muscle fiber integrity. Combined MSCs + BA treatment improved several biochemical and histological outcomes compared with exercise alone. Serum lactate concentrations remained elevated in treated groups 24 h after the final exercise session, indicating altered post-exercise metabolic responses. Overall, intramuscular BA modulated metabolic responses, whereas administration of bone marrow-derived stromal/stem cell-like cells was associated with structural regeneration in this rat model of exercise-induced skeletal muscle injury, providing a reproducible platform for evaluating regenerative interventions.

metadata.title: Aerobic Exercise Ameliorates Osteoarthritic Chondrocyte Degradation in Osteoarthritis via Regulating E2F8/NLRP14 Signaling Pathway.
metadata.abstract: Although physical activity is known to mitigate disease risks, its protective molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. E2F8, a regulator of cell cycle and metabolism, showed significant differential expression between osteoarthritis (OA) and exercise models, suggesting it may link mechanical activity to OA alleviation. In vitro, Interleukin-1 Beta (IL-1β) simulated inflammation. In vivo, OA was induced in rats via Monosodium iodoacetate (MIA) injection. The effects of E2F8 and mechanical stress were assessed using moderate treadmill exercise, histology, and joint observation. Bioinformatic analysis, cyclic tensile strain, Western blot, immunofluorescence, and gene knockdown were used to investigate mechanisms. In OA rats, E2F8 was downregulated in cartilage while NLRP14 increased. Exercise reversed E2F8 downregulation, alleviated cartilage degeneration, restored anabolic activity, and reduced inflammatory catabolism linked to senescence. In vitro, mechanical stress reversed the IL-1β-induced anabolic/catabolic imbalance by regulating the E2F8/NLRP14, mitigating OA progression. Mechanical stress enhances E2F8 expression in osteoarthritic chondrocytes, which in turn protects cartilage by suppressing the expression of NLRP14. These findings underscore the role of E2F8 as a mechano-sensitive mediator and highlight the potential of exercise or exercise-mimetic therapies as effective strategies for preventing and treating OA.

metadata.title: Strontium- and magnesium-doped hydroxyapatite scaffolds enhance bone regeneration by promoting macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype.
metadata.abstract: The development of synthetic bone grafts that integrate osteogenic and immunomodulatory functions represents a critical strategy in regenerative orthopedics. In this study, we fabricated strontium- and magnesium-doped hydroxyapatite (HA/Mg/Sr) scaffolds derived from natural bovine cancellous bone. Physicochemical characterization confirmed the preservation of a three-dimensional interconnected porous architecture (∼80% porosity, ∼350 μm pore size) with a homogeneous nanoparticulate surface. Doping with Mg and Sr enhanced scaffold degradation, sustained the release of bioactive ions (,,), and significantly increased compressive strength to levels comparable with human cancellous bone.In vitro, HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds exhibited excellent biocompatibility, promoting adhesion and proliferation of both bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs). While Mg primarily facilitated direct osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs, Sr played a dominant role in directing macrophage polarization toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, as evidenced by increased CD206 and IL-10 expression alongside reduced CCR7 and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α). Notably, macrophage-conditioned medium from HA/Mg/Sr cultures substantially enhanced BMSC osteogenesis, highlighting immunomodulation as a central mechanism. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that the HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds promoted macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype and modulated immune responses potentially through the NF-κB signaling pathway, which was validated by Western blot. In a rat femoral condyle defect model, HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds-particularly those with 10% Sr content (HA/Mg/Sr2)-demonstrated superior bone regeneration, characterized by bone volume fraction (BV/TV), trabecular thickness (Tb.Th), trabecular number (Tb.N) and enhanced new bone ingrowth and integration, accompanied by elevated M2 macrophage infiltrationin vivo. Overall, these findings establish that HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds promote bone repair not only via direct osteoconduction but, more importantly, through immunomodulation-fostering a pro-healing M2 macrophage microenvironment potentially in an NF-κB-dependent manner, thereby offering a promising dual-functional biomaterial strategy for critical-sized bone defect reconstruction. Collectively, this study underscores the therapeutic relevance of targeting macrophage polarization in bone repair and delineates a mechanistic framework for Sr-based immunomodulatory biomaterial design.

metadata.title: Role of integrin αvβ5 receptor and microglia in delayed-onset muscle soreness in mice.
metadata.abstract: Delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) is characterized by muscle pain, stiffness, and tenderness following intense or unaccustomed exercise. In humans, symptoms typically arise 6-72 h post-exercise. This study investigated a novel mechanism underlying DOMS, focusing on the involvement of the irisin receptor integrin αvβ5 and spinal microglia in its development. Male C57BL/6 mice were subjected to a DOMS model induced by an acute aerobic exercise protocol, and nociceptive thresholds were assessed using the von Frey filament test. The role of spinal integrin αvβ5 was evaluated via intrathecal administration of the antagonist cilengitide, given both prior to exercise and 24 h post-exercise. To assess irisin's nociceptive effects, it was also administered intrathecally. Additionally, minocycline, a microglial inhibitor, was administered before irisin to determine microglial involvement. An in vitro assay evaluated microglial activation by irisin via flow cytometry. Pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines were quantified by ELISA. Cilengitide reversed exercise-induced DOMS and reduced spinal pro-inflammatory cytokines. Irisin induced nociception, which was attenuated by minocycline. Irisin also activated microglia in vitro, increasing pro-inflammatory cytokine production. These findings suggest integrin αvβ5 and spinal microglia play critical roles in DOMS pathogenesis, with irisin and pro-inflammatory cytokines as key mediators.

metadata.title: Superiority of Tetrapeptide Tyr-Gly-Leu-Phe over Amino Acid Mixture: Mechanisms Underlying Enhanced Systemic Amino Acid Delivery, Anti-Fatigue Efficacy, and Muscle Damage Repair.
metadata.abstract: This study compared the anti-fatigue tetrapeptide YGLF with an equimolar amino acid (AA) mixture across three stages: postingestion absorption, postexercise fatigue, and muscle damage repair. Despite rapid in vitro degradation (<1% intact), YGLF elevated plasma AAs more effectively than the AA mixture 15 min postingestion (51.97 vs 46.34 mg/100 mL). Postexercise, YGLF outperformed the AA mixture by further increasing muscle AAs and blood glucose, reducing metabolic byproducts, and activating AMPK. Following muscle damage, transcriptomics revealed that the AA mixture primarily modulated energy metabolism, whereas YGLF uniquely upregulated muscle growth genes. Western blotting confirmed that YGLF promoted repair via the Sestrin2/mTOR and Pax7/MYOD pathways. These findings demonstrate the distinct bioactivity of YGLF over that of free AAs, establishing a rationale for utilizing specific peptides in sports nutrition and muscle recovery.

metadata.title: WNT5A-Associated Osteogenic Enhancement Contributes to the Protective Effects of OPG-Fc in Glucocorticoid-Associated Femoral Head Osteonecrosis.
metadata.abstract: Steroid-induced osteonecrosis of the femoral head (SONFH) is a progressive orthopedic disorder characterized by an imbalance between bone resorption and bone formation. Although receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa-B ligand (RANKL) blockers are known to suppress osteoclast activity, whether they also promote osteogenesis and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated whether osteoprotegerin-Fc (OPG-Fc) exerts osteoprotective effects in SONFH and whether wingless-type MMTV integration site family, member 5A (WNT5A) signaling is involved. A rat SONFH model was established using lipopolysaccharide (LPS) combined with methylprednisolone sodium succinate (MPS), and bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) were cultured under glucocorticoid-containing conditions. OPG-Fc, the WNT5A antagonist box5, and Wnt5a knockdown were used, and analyses included micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), histological staining, transcriptome sequencing, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), and western blotting. Our results demonstrated that OPG-Fc significantly improved bone trabecular microarchitecture, reduced empty lacunae and tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP)-positive cells, and increased cartilage thickness in vivo. In vitro, OPG-Fc promoted osteogenic differentiation while inhibiting adipogenic differentiation of BMSCs. Transcriptome and protein analyses revealed significantly higher WNT5A expression following OPG-Fc treatment. Importantly, pharmacological blockade of WNT5A with box5 and Wnt5a knockdown partially attenuated OPG-Fc-associated pro-osteogenic effects, whereas box5 had limited effects on anti-resorptive marker changes. These findings suggest that OPG-Fc exerts dual protective actions in SONFH by suppressing bone resorption and enhancing osteogenic differentiation in association with WNT5A-related signaling. This study provides new mechanistic insights into RANKL blockade therapy and offers a potential molecular target for early intervention in SONFH.

metadata.title: Delphinidin induces the upregulation of miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle and miR-23a-3p release from intestinal cells.
metadata.abstract: Delphinidin, one of the major anthocyanidins, inhibits disuse muscle atrophy by increasing the expression of miR-23a-3p in mouse skeletal muscle. However, delphinidin is less stable and poorly absorbed in vivo, so its mechanism of function remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which delphinidin increases miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle. miRNAs can be packaged into extracellular vesicles (EVs) and secreted from cells. We investigated whether delphinidin induces the release of miR-23a-3p encapsulated in EVs from intestinal cells and whether these EVs increase miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle cells. A single dose of delphinidin increased the expression of miR-23a-3p in the small intestine of mice. To examine whether delphinidin affects the secretion of miR-23a-3p in intestinal cells, we used differentiated Caco-2 cells as an in vitro model. Results showed that delphinidin increases the expression of miR-23a-3p in EVs secreted from differentiated Caco-2 cells. In addition, EVs derived from delphinidin-treated Caco-2 cells were taken up by differentiated C2C12 myotubes, resulting in increased intracellular miR-23a-3p expression. Our in vitro results suggest that intestinal cell-derived EVs may contribute to the antimuscle atrophy activity of delphinidin through the delivery of miR-23a-3p to skeletal muscle cells.

metadata.title: Myogenic differentiation-derived small extracellular vesicles as a therapeutic strategy for miR-193b-3p-mediated muscle regeneration.
metadata.abstract: The regeneration of skeletal muscle involves precisely regulated intercellular communication, including extracellular vesicle (EV)-mediated processes. In this study, we show that during in vitro myogenic differentiation of human skeletal muscle progenitor cells (myoblasts), miR-193b-3p accumulates within small EVs (sEVs) in a temporally regulated manner. Both sEV-mediated and synthetic delivery of miR-193b-3p enhanced myogenic differentiation in vitro and promoted histological recovery in a murine volumetric muscle loss model. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that miR-193b-3p directly suppresses adapter-related protein complex 2 subunit mu 1 (AP2M1), a clathrin-associated adapter protein that has not been well characterized in muscle biology, and identify it as a negative regulator of myogenic progression. AP2M1 knockdown phenocopied the effects of miR-193b-3p, suggesting that this regulatory axis may contribute to muscle regeneration. In addition, transcriptomic analyses of aged rodent and sarcopenic human datasets revealed conserved upregulation of AP2M1 in degenerative muscle states, supporting its potential clinical relevance. Collectively, these findings reveal a myogenic differentiation-dependent, sEV-mediated miRNA regulatory mechanism that contributes to muscle regeneration. Based on these results, we propose the miR-193b-3p-AP2M1 axis as a potential therapeutic target for muscle-wasting disorders.

metadata.title: Laser-programmed anisotropic hierarchical host bone interfaces for mechanotransduction-guided osseointegration.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Conventional mechanical osteotomy often induces thermal and mechanical damage, which compromises the biological quality of the host bone interface and impairs subsequent osseointegration. This study aimed to develop a 9.3 μm CO2 laser-based osteotomy strategy that integrates precise bone cutting with in situ regenerative interface engineering. METHODS: A 9.3 μm CO2 laser osteotomy platform was developed by combining controlled pulse-overlap scanning with gas-atomized water-mist cooling. The generated osteotomy interfaces were characterized in terms of surface topography, thermal response, microstructural preservation, and local mechanical integrity. Human mesenchymal stem cell (hMSC) alignment, focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, osteogenic differentiation, and osteoclast formation were evaluated in vitro. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses were performed to investigate the underlying molecular programs. The optimized interface was further assessed in a rat femoral defect model with porous titanium scaffold implantation. RESULTS: The laser osteotomy strategy generated deterministic microscale grooves and graded nanoscale roughness, forming anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano osteotomy interfaces. Compared with mechanical cutting, laser osteotomy reduced thermal accumulation, limited microstructural disruption, and better maintained local mechanical integrity. The engineered interfaces directed hMSC alignment and activated focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, as indicated by enhanced pFAK activation, Lamin A/C reinforcement, and YAP nuclear translocation. These responses promoted osteogenic differentiation and suppressed osteoclast formation, with the Laser III group showing the most favorable biological response. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses further revealed enrichment of adhesion-, cytoskeleton-, and PI3K-Akt-related osteogenic programs. In vivo, the optimized interface enhanced peri-implant bone regeneration, mineral apposition, and osseointegration. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides proof-of-concept evidence that 9.3 μm CO2 laser osteotomy may enable bone cutting to be coupled with in situ regenerative interface engineering. By reducing cutting-associated damage and actively programming the host bone interface, this approach shows translational potential for improving peri-implant bone healing and implant integration. THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL OF THIS ARTICLE: 9.3 μm CO2 laser-enabled osteotomy interface engineering integrates precise bone cutting with in situ programming of the host bone surface. This study reveals that laser-generated anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano interfaces can reduce cutting-associated damage, activate adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, promote osteogenic differentiation, suppress osteoclast maturation, and enhance peri-implant osseointegration. These findings provide a regenerative osteotomy strategy for improving the biological quality of surgically created bone interfaces, which holds translational potential for orthopedic implant surgery, fracture reconstruction, and the repair of bone defects in clinical practice.

metadata.title: Chaenomeles speciosa-derived extracellular vesicles accelerate fracture healing via orchestrating immuno-angiogenic coupling.
metadata.abstract: PURPOSE: Fracture nonunion remains a major orthopaedic challenge, and dysregulation of the bone immune microenvironment is increasingly recognized as a key pathological driver. Chaenomeles speciosa is a medicinal plant with documented anti-inflammatory properties, making it a promising candidate for immune-modulatory therapy. This study investigated whether extracellular vesicles derived from Chaenomeles speciosa could reshape the immune microenvironment to promote fracture healing. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on human nonunion tissues to characterize cellular heterogeneity. Network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses were used to identify potential therapeutic targets of Chaenomeles speciosa. Extracellular vesicles were isolated by ultracentrifugation and characterized by transmission electron microscopy. Macrophage polarization, angiogenesis, and inflammatory signaling were assessed in vitro using RAW 264.7 macrophages and human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Bone regeneration was evaluated in a rat femoral fracture model using micro-computed tomography and histology. RESULTS: Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed M1 macrophage dominance and enhanced M1-mediated communication with osteoblasts and endothelial cells in nonunion tissues. The IL-17 signaling pathway and matrix metalloproteinase-3 were identified as key therapeutic targets. Isolated extracellular vesicles exhibited excellent biocompatibility, promoted M2 macrophage polarization, attenuated inflammation, and enhanced angiogenesis in vitro. In the rat fracture model, treatment with these extracellular vesicles significantly accelerated bone regeneration, as evidenced by increased bone bridging and callus formation. CONCLUSION: These findings establish a macrophage-centric pathological network in nonunion and demonstrate that Chaenomeles speciosa-derived extracellular vesicles promote bone repair through immuno-angiogenic coupling, supporting their potential as a multi-targeted therapeutic strategy for fracture healing.
